title: Render System block diagrams from hosted TSX and Circuit JSON
description: Add support for rendering system block diagrams in SVG and PNG formats, including manifest generation and page selection.
body:
Hosted `systemblock` examples currently fail because the service does not accept a System view and its pinned core/renderer predate System diagrams.

Add `svg_type=system` / `view=system` for SVG and PNG using the existing compressed-code, file-map, and Circuit JSON inputs. `system_page` selects a 1-based page; `system_manifest=true` lists page names and IDs. Generated URL pages include System image and manifest links. Page headers survive svg3 cache hits; svg3 routes these requests through the shared container renderer.

Update the core pin and override to 0.0.2261, props to 0.0.717, Circuit JSON to 0.0.543, and circuit-to-svg to 0.0.455.

Validation:
- Full suite: 121 pass, one existing skip, no failures.
- Production build/typecheck and complete production smoke tests under both Bun and Node pass, including System TSX, PNG, manifests, and invalid selections.
- svg3 typecheck, 34 tests, 12 real Worker/native rendering comparisons, and deployment/container dry run pass.
- New SVG snapshots cover the exact docs example and a selected power-diagram page.

Prerequisite for merging https://github.com/tscircuit/docs/pull/980. The docs PR remains open.

title: Fix homepage RP2040 interactive 3D model loading
description: Fixes the issue where clicking the RP2040 board on the homepage results in a loading error, by adding a functional 3D model that loads correctly upon interaction.
body:
Clicking the RP2040 board on the homepage leaves the viewer stuck loading. The preview supplies only an image, with no circuit input for the generated GLB URL, and the viewer collapses to zero height after replacing the image, preventing its lazy loader from requesting any model.

Add an optional `threeDModelUrl` and a self-contained GLB generated from the same pinned board release as the image. Preserve a visible viewport when switching to the model. The GLB is fetched only after clicking; exploded poses continue using their generated models. The existing preview generation script now also writes the matching GLB.

Validation: all 27 tests pass, TypeScript passes, and the production build passes. Chromium checks at 1280px and 390px confirm no model request before clicking, a successful GLB response, `model-viewer.loaded`, and camera rotation by dragging. Added regression coverage for prebuilt model loading without POSTing circuit data and retaining exploded-pose behavior. Vercel deployment succeeded; verified the deployed homepage loads the GLB and has a visible 818 × 613.5 viewport.

[Preview the homepage](https://docs-git-fix-homepage-3d-model-tscircuit.vercel.app/).

title: Document assembly face mounting and hole-fastened bolts
description: The assembly docs still say generic parts have no mounting props, and the PCB screw guide manually copies hole coordinates. There are no element references for assembly.bolt or assembly.referencesurface. Add those references and update the existing part, subassembly, printed-part, motor and assembly guides for the merged API. The examples cover CSS face selectors, target-local signed offsets, normal clearance, geometry-less groups, inherited frames, and topbottom fastening to plain and plated PCB holes. Fasteners use canonical modelprinter strings such as hexsocketbolt_m3_l10mm; mechanical holes use authored datums rather than mesh inference. Three complete shared sources power the CircuitPreview code, editor links, generated Circuit JSON and four inspected 3D views. The bearing housing has explicit pocket and hole geometry, and the bolt model comes from JSCAD Electronics. No GLB assets are added. The generator fails on unavailable model URLs instead of silently publishing placeholder geometry. Validation: all three examples built with the published tscircuit0.0.3064 CLI, and their emitted geometry matches the documented seating planes and group offsets. All 26 docs tests, TypeScript, formatting, and relative-link checks passed. The production site build and all GitHub checks passed. All eight preview routes and all four rendered PNG assets return HTTP 200.  Updated page  Verified deployment preview   ---  ---   Bolts  Open page(https:docs-git-codex-assembly-mounting-docs-tscircuit.vercel.appelementsassembly-bolt)   Reference surfaces  Open page(https:docs-git-codex-assembly-mounting-docs-tscircuit.vercel.appelementsassembly-referencesurface)   Parts  Open page(https:docs-git-codex-assembly-mounting-docs-tscircuit.vercel.appelementsassembly-part)   Subassemblies  Open page(https:docs-git-codex-assembly-mounting-docs-tscircuit.vercel.appelementsassembly-subassembly)   Printed parts  Open page(https:docs-git-codex-assembly-mounting-docs-tscircuit.vercel.appelementsassembly-printedpart)   Motors  Open page(https:docs-git-codex-assembly-mounting-docs-tscircuit.vercel.appelementsassembly-motor)   Mounting 3D models  Open page(https:docs-git-codex-assembly-mounting-docs-tscircuit.vercel.appguidestscircuit-essentialsmounting-3d-models)   Advanced Assembly  Open page(https:docs-git-codex-assembly-mounting-docs-tscircuit.vercel.appguidesadvanced-assembly)
body:
The assembly docs still say generic parts have no mounting props, and the PCB screw guide manually copies hole coordinates. There are no element references for `assembly.bolt` or `assembly.referencesurface`.

Add those references and update the existing part, subassembly, printed-part, motor and assembly guides for the merged API. The examples cover CSS face selectors, target-local signed offsets, normal clearance, geometry-less groups, inherited frames, and top/bottom fastening to plain and plated PCB holes. Fasteners use canonical modelprinter strings such as `hexsocketbolt_m3_l10mm`; mechanical holes use authored datums rather than mesh inference.

Three complete shared sources power the CircuitPreview code, editor links, generated Circuit JSON and four inspected 3D views. The bearing housing has explicit pocket and hole geometry, and the bolt model comes from JSCAD Electronics. No GLB assets are added. The generator fails on unavailable model URLs instead of silently publishing placeholder geometry.

Validation: all three examples built with the published `tscircuit@0.0.3064` CLI, and their emitted geometry matches the documented seating planes and group offsets. All 26 docs tests, TypeScript, formatting, and relative-link checks passed. The production site build and all GitHub checks passed. All eight preview routes and all four rendered PNG assets return HTTP 200.

Stacked on #3524. The unchanged real H3 input now reports DQS1P as disconnected after **80,473 iterations instead of 2,000,000**. DDR routing completion is unchanged.

title: fix: pin repair03 with physical copper contact protection
description: Fixes pin repair03 to prevent new physical trace-to-via shorts while preserving exact via anchors and existing repair search budgets.
body:
Pin repair03 to `8ec1f3acf1c5f2b228e6f6d8c8972d4ee2045962` to prevent new physical trace-to-via shorts while preserving exact via anchors, circular pad geometry and the existing repair search budgets. Current main (`9978773`), including the H3 DDR terminal-pad fix, is merged.

Remove repeated work from repair: reuse exact primitive geometry within the existing DRC cache budget; copy errors once at the public-result boundary; reject proven pad-overlap proposals before full-board DRC; prune distant board edges and use numeric spatial-grid columns. The consumer caches connected multilayer obstacles and indexes preloaded routes once per candidate. Every surviving candidate still receives complete validation; candidate order and search budgets are unchanged.

Dataset01 P50 follow-up at the same base and PR commits: the [independent official rerun](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3496#issuecomment-6659996153) is **1,326.1 → 1,308.0 ms (-1.37%)**, with total runtime +0.18%, 85/85 solved and zero DRC issues. No production code or benchmark settings changed for this follow-up. The original +11.50% observation is retained in the table below.

A [predetermined three-round comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/42041529531) ran all 85 cases nine times with identical non-repair dependencies, Bun 1.4.2, concurrency 3, threads 1 and effort 1. Execution orders were main/PR/control, PR/control/main, then control/main/PR; control is an identical copy of main. Every round is reported:

| Round | Main P50 | PR P50 | Identical main P50 | PR vs mean controls |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1315.5 ms | 1388.8 ms | 1284.2 ms | +6.84% |
| 2 | 1305.8 ms | 1382.9 ms | 1396.0 ms | +2.37% |
| 3 | 1304.7 ms | 1306.4 ms | 1307.4 ms | +0.03% |

Across repeated per-case medians, the median paired case change is +0.92%; the dataset P50 of those per-case medians is 1292.6 → 1382.9 ms (+6.98%). Total runtime against both controls changes +1.62%, +0.01%, +1.01%. All 85 SVG outputs match in every pass. Earlier fixed main/PR repeats measured P50 -10.34% / -9.84%, and identical-main controls alone differed by -9.53% in one pair. The distribution remains sensitive; these results do not establish a persistent +11.5% slowdown or prove zero overhead.

In the original run, sample 31 moved from rank 42 to 44, changing the median from sample 8 (1,306.0 ms) to sample 14 (1,456.1 ms). Sample 14 itself was 1,460.4 ms on main. Of sample 31's 188.3 ms extra runtime, only 2.8 ms was in the modified global/joint repair stages; the rest was elsewhere, mainly unchanged routing and simplification stages. In the new balanced comparison, sample 31's repeated median is still +7.45% (+95.8 ms), with +0.9 ms in those repair stages. These measurements do not identify a repair-stage change that explains the remaining case slowdown; no production patch was made for this follow-up.

Initial same-machine comparisons at this head use main `9978773` and PR `a613b05`, Pipeline9, effort 1, three isolated sample processes and Bun 1.4.2 on Blacksmith. Negative timing changes are faster. Solved time sums only the same successfully solved cases, so existing timeouts cannot hide a slowdown.

| Dataset | Solved | DRC issues | Solved time Δ | P50 time Δ | Memory P50 Δ | Memory P90 Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/42032093211) | 85 → 85 | 0 → 0 | +1.04% | +11.50% | -0.28% | +0.85% |
| [SRJ18](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/42032112678) | 16 → 16 | 0 → 0 | -1.55% | -1.16% | +0.67% | -0.11% |
| [SRJ33](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/42032092747) | 35 → 35 | 137 → 137 | -2.24% | -0.19% | -2.09% | -0.97% |
| [SRJ24](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/42032085910) | 19 → 19 | 64 → 64 | -2.30% | -2.35% | +4.87% | +0.40% |

No new per-case DRC, completion, timeout, via-count or trace-lint regressions. SRJ24 retains its six existing timeouts. SVG outputs match except SRJ33 sample 36's intended contact-repair change, covered by the publication-safety and repair-budget regression test.

[Fixed two-pair repeats](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/42032025047), with identical non-repair dependencies and both execution orders:

| Base | Dataset | Total time Δ, base-first / PR-first |
|---|---|---:|
| Previous PR head `e674cc8` | dataset01 | +0.91% / +1.62% |
| Current main | dataset01 | -3.35% / -3.92% |
| Previous PR head `e674cc8` | srj18 | +0.97% / +1.76% |
| Current main | srj18 | +0.58% / +3.39% |
| Current main | srj33 | -2.00% / -3.38% |

[Identical-main controls](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/42033052327) bracket the PR between two copies of main on the same runner. Against their average, dataset01 changes +0.45% / -1.84%; SRJ18 changes -0.02% / -1.01%. Identical-main total time itself changes -3.46% / -1.87% for dataset01 and +0.26% / +7.39% for SRJ18. These controls quantify the measured spread; the slower PR repeats above are retained.

Sample 15's whole-process RSS remains intermittent. The official SRJ18 comparison is 2,586 → 5,126 MiB; two additional main/PR pairs are 5,204 → 2,556 and 5,048 → 2,689 MiB. In the identical-main controls, the same source and dependencies produce 5,345 vs 2,715 and 5,330 vs 2,655 MiB. A [fixed six-pass phase check](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/42034174458) ranges 2,578–2,661 MiB across main, PR and identical main; all peaks occur in the unchanged high-density force-improvement stage, before modified repair, final DRC and SVG generation. The roughly 5 GiB spike also occurs on main; these results do not establish a PR-specific doubling or eliminate the existing peak-memory instability.

Validation: all 186 repair tests / 50,526 assertions and both repair TypeScript projects pass. Consumer integration passes six tests / 637 assertions and typecheck, including unchanged full Game Boy geometry, Game Boy/SRJ33 repair-work budgets, exact via anchors, physical-contact publication safety and H3 DDR pads. Final-head hosted CI is green and both PRs are conflict-free.

Its complete Git tree is identical to the previously validated `4831877` pin (`32db0d94ef183c04972bf9c6fe4194f58ae3fd97`). The repair avoids repeated native DRC evaluations and common broad-force passes, and skips exact projections for distant contact pairs. Search budgets and candidate acceptance are unchanged.

The branch includes current main `41673fb`, preserves the pad-drill, plated-hole, exact via-anchor, and circular-SMT geometry fixes, and includes the circular-SMT consumer regression test. This pin now follows repair03 main after the performance PR merged.

Validation: **165 repair tests / 41,347 assertions** and repair typecheck pass locally; **7 focused consumer tests / 678 assertions** pass. Before this content-identical pin update, consumer CI passed all **9 test shards**, build, typecheck, format, dependency/string-ID guards, and Vercel build. Repair CI tests, typecheck, and format pass. CI will rerun on the new pin-only commit; no solver code changed.

Official `/benchmark --same-machine --dataset ...` comments were posted as **techmannih**, using `dataset01`, `18`, `33`, and `24`. All requested full datasets have completed. The benchmark keeps the existing effort, concurrency, timeouts, DRC checks, and memory measurement.

| Dataset / full round | Runtime P50 | Runtime P95 | Memory P50 | Memory P80 | Memory P90 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41911866555) | +0.83% | -5.04% | -2.46% | +0.08% | -0.81% |
| [SRJ18 round 1](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41911368147) | -0.08% | +1.07% | -0.43% | +10.27% | +2.31% |
| [SRJ18 round 2](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41913816088) | +2.48% | +0.30% | -1.53% | -2.60% | -0.12% |
| [SRJ18 round 3](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41913813904) | +0.17% | -1.36% | -0.80% | -5.57% | -2.28% |
| [SRJ24](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41911867708) | +2.43% | +0.00% | -2.03% | +1.07% | -3.29% |
| [SRJ33](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41911857916) | -1.44% | -0.64% | +1.07% | +4.16% | -3.67% |

The screenshot's **+8.8% was Memory P80**, not runtime. It came from SRJ18 `sample014`. Three predefined current full-cohort rounds measure **+10.27%, -2.60%, -5.57%** at Memory P80 (median **-2.60%**); `sample014` occupies P80 in every round. These observations do not support a stable +8.8% increase, but the unfavorable first round remains included. Three isolated repeats were +4.00%, -2.13%, +0.04%; those single-sample runs do not replace the full-cohort comparisons. A universal zero-increase memory/runtime gate is not established.

The original reviewed SRJ33 ordinal 32 is `sample051`. The current full benchmark measures **29.737 → 28.238 seconds (-5.04%)**; global repair **2.595 → 1.321 seconds (-49.09%)**. Routing outcomes are unchanged.

Across the four full datasets, all **164 board outcomes** are unchanged, including completion, timeout status, DRC counts/types, vias, and trace-lint counts. SRJ24's existing failures/timeouts remain in the report; its timeout-penalized P95 is not a successful-board tail measurement.

Provenance: base consumer `41673fb0cd159303cc68796e9fe4d04692b92a8e`; first full rounds use consumer `079d7f2`, while the two SRJ18 repeats and isolated checks use the previously tested `9b5a12b`. Those consumer heads differ only in the repair pin: old `e62f85a`, pre-merge `4831877`, and merged main `cac186e` have the **identical complete Git tree** `32db0d94ef183c04972bf9c6fe4194f58ae3fd97`. Bun 1.4.2, Blacksmith ARM, three concurrent samples, one routing thread, effort 1, 360-second sample timeout.

Older [controlled performance measurements](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41689685997) used earlier frozen revisions and remain historical evidence, separate from the current results above.

Additional diagnostics also retain unfavorable results. [Two opposite-order ablation rounds](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41913426200) measured base/fix peaks of 2118/2061 MiB in round 1 and 2055/3256 MiB in round 2; disabling duplicate checks also produced a 3134 MiB peak. The initial timer hook only recorded start/end because inline routing blocked the timer.

A [follow-up with direct stage-boundary recording](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41916229436) measured base/fix peaks of 2015/2062 MiB and 2020/3130 MiB. In its large-gap round, current RSS was already **1770 vs 2824 MiB before global repair**, and **1789 vs 2844 MiB after global repair**. The gap appeared during port-point pathing/high-density routing, before the changed force-candidate paths ran. Thus the large observed gap is not evidence that the resumable broad-force runner itself retained that extra GiB. All diagnostic routing outcomes remain unchanged. These instrumented, isolated runs are separate from the official full-cohort table.

The precise allocator/GC cause remains unconfirmed, and intermittent RSS spikes are **not claimed fixed**. The latest pushed update only switches the dependency pin to the content-identical merged main commit. No additional memory-specific algorithm change was made.

title: perf: reduce Pipeline9 clearance projection cost via repair04
description: Reduces the clearance projection cost in Pipeline9 by optimizing the underlying calculations in repair04, resulting in significant performance improvements without altering the existing DRC utilities.
body:
Pipeline9's clearance projection lives in repair04. Pin `@tscircuit/repair04` to `57763abb9b086c0a556499b806a95cb6e371435b` from https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/pull/62. The entire autorouter diff is one line in `package.json`; DRC utilities stay unchanged.

### What the reviewer can verify

The upstream diff replaces all-pairs preparation with spatial queries, filters discarded indices before sorting, and simplifies rectangular point/via distance to the same existing clamp/distance calculation. It removes the dense-case bounds cache and retains baseline projection arithmetic. No clearance, sweep count, physical validation or search budget is relaxed.

The upstream PR commits a reproducible benchmark using all 13 existing real repro inputs and the unchanged legacy output hashes. It runs five alternating fresh-process pairs and reports every case, raw runs and work counters. Prepared pairs drop 10,068,159 → 675,670 (-93.3%). See [the code, complete per-case table and reproduction command](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/pull/62).

### Current dependency-only results

Base `37c2ed8` versus head `d3d19fa`; Apple M4 / Bun 1.3.14. Full routing uses SRJ18, Pipeline9, effort 1, one worker and one routing thread. Full-suite order is PR → base; replay orders alternate.

| Measurement | Base | Updated repair04 | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Projection, all 13 real repros, five-run median | 605.344ms | 409.029ms | **-32.4%** |
| Captured sample015 joint DRC, three-run median | 9.590s | 6.792s | **-29.2%** |
| Full SRJ18 joint DRC, all 16 boards | 35.354s | 28.171s | **-20.3%** |
| Full routing P50 | 10.862s | 10.904s | +0.4% |
| Full routing P95 | 41.215s | 41.434s | +0.5% |
| Full routing total | 250.895s | 252.116s | +0.5% |

All 13 projection-case medians and all 16 full-suite joint DRC stages are faster. Both full-suite revisions solve 16/16 with zero DRC issues/timeouts, identical via/lint results and byte-identical route SVGs. All 11 captured projection inputs retain byte-identical routes; the joint replay keeps 465 attempts, 164221 search nodes and 12 top-level reference validations.

The optimization is concrete in the changed projection/DRC work. This local pair does not demonstrate an overall routing-time win; that claim is deliberately excluded.

### CI status

Latest upstream format/type/test and benchmark jobs are queued. Two fresh matched integration comparisons are also queued: [run 1](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41862441532), [run 2](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41862461924). Each runs base and PR sequentially on one Blacksmith runner. They will publish their own result comments and raw artifacts when runners become available.

This PR remains draft while CI and upstream review are pending. Local focused source type checking, unchanged geometry SHA tests and the 11,325 exact point-distance comparisons pass. Four pre-existing local SVG snapshot mismatches are also present on the baseline and were not changed.

body:
Fixes https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-step/issues/176. Unblocks https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/issues/5661 after publication and CLI consumption.

The copper pad is oval, but its drill can be circular. Equal drill width/height leaves zero-length straight walls in the slot exporter; normalizing them produces NaN directions (0.0.47) or `STEP real must be finite` (0.0.62). Route round pill drills through the existing circular-hole exporter, preserving offsets. Non-round slots keep their original path. No tolerance workaround, swallowed error, skipped valid hole or dependency change is added.

Stack: repro #179 → fix #177. Preview the combined change against main: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-step/stack/180

**One simple top-down 3D snapshot, updated in place:** this PR modifies `test/basics/basics24/__snapshots__/basics24.snap.png`, introduced by the repro. The oval pad and round drill are visible together beside slotted/circular controls. Both before/after use identical framing and explicitly labelled reference copper pads. Before shows the working control substrate because the full input produces no STEP; after shows the actual successfully exported substrate with all three holes. No 2D PCB image, full LoRa fixture, additional snapshot, or copper-export feature is introduced by this fix.

Native CAD checks verify the actual unadorned STEP separately from the reference-pad display: finite coordinates, successful OCCT import, openings through both PCB faces and surrounding material retained. The existing separate pad-variants test is changed from recording failure to verifying successful import/through-hole coverage; it adds no image.

Validation: **53 tests pass, 775 assertions**; typecheck, library/declaration build, formatting and diff checks pass. Before/after snapshots visually inspected.

Downstream: CLI #5663 must consume the actual fixed published converter. Current 0.0.62 alone is insufficient. No preview/link versions are committed. Nothing merged or released.

title: repro: round pill drills prevent STEP export (#176)
description: Reproduces the failure of round pill drills during STEP export, providing a test case and validation for the issue.
body:
Reproduces https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-step/issues/176 and the converter failure behind https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/issues/5661.

Minimal case: a 10×6×1.6 mm board with three plated holes, no components:
- Left: oval/pill pad 1.7×1.95 mm, round drill 0.95×0.95 mm (fails).
- Middle: same pad, slotted drill 0.95×1.2 mm (control).
- Right: circular pad and round 0.95 mm drill (control).

**Top-down 3D → 3D:** the snapshot shows copper pad shapes as explicitly labelled reference geometry from the same fixture. These display-only references are not added to production STEP files. The full input throws `STEP real must be finite` on published 0.0.62, so its actual failed output cannot be rendered. The before substrate therefore comes from the two working controls only, clearly labelled; the failed left drill has no corresponding substrate hole. Do not interpret this control model as a file produced by the failed export.

The snapshot is introduced here at `test/basics/basics24/__snapshots__/basics24.snap.png`. Fix #177 updates that exact file with the successful actual substrate/drills and the same reference pads, renderer, top-down camera and lighting. No separate fixed snapshot or duplicate full-board case remains.

The separate pad-variants regression records the same error for other supported pad shapes. Its source data also lives in this repro. The independent full-board repro #175 is untouched.

Validation: both repro tests pass, including genuine failure assertions and native OCCT import of the controls/reference scene; typecheck and formatting pass.

Preview stack against main: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-step/stack/180
Review/merge repro #179 and fix #177 together through the native stack.

title: Fix shared rail corners and blocked power label placement
description: Fixes placement of shared rail corners and ensures proper positioning of power labels to avoid overlaps and collisions in the schematic layout.
body:
The RVboy Advance SOC repro from #1403 now places V3V3 at the shared rail corner, moves the rail 0.3 mm toward the pins while retaining 0.1 mm clearance from USB_1V8, and places CODEC_VCM entirely outside the rail. CODEC_1V8 moves farther left so CODEC_VCM keeps a single-elbow connector without crossing either label.

title: fix: round polygon clipping coordinates to KiCad precision (#814)
description: Fixes polygon clipping issues by rounding coordinates to KiCads 1 nm precision, preventing crashes during cutout operations.
body:
Fixes #814. Stacked on #831; merge the reproduction PR first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

The 2 × 2 tab-routed panel crashes when rotated cutouts produce nearly coincident polygon edges (for example, `1.0000000000000009` instead of `1`). Rectangular boards fail while assembling an output ring; rounded boards fail in the sweep-line tree.

Round the board and cutout polygon coordinates to [KiCad's documented 1 nm PCB resolution](https://dev-docs.kicad.org/en/file-formats/sexpr-intro/#_board_coordinates) before the existing clipping operation. Round its output to the same precision so the existing zero-length segment check also removes intersections that coincide in KiCad. The source Circuit JSON is unchanged. This uses the existing stage/helper pattern and clipping dependency, with no catch-and-continue, retries, or panel-specific geometry exceptions.

Replace the repro's expected-failure assertions with successful conversion, unchanged input, preserved component footprints, and closed, finite, nonzero Edge.Cuts checks. Update both stacked snapshots and add a regression ensuring a 1 nm-wide cutout is retained. The snapshots use the unchanged helper and its existing `--page-size-mode 2` board-area framing. Since only the first board currently has an outline (#813), the KiCad image is cropped to that board; all eight component footprints remain in the exported PCB and are asserted by the regression. Neither snapshot helper is changed.

**Scope:** #813 remains separate. Export now completes, but the existing converter still emits only the first board's outline; the updated snapshots intentionally show that limitation.

title: Stop the animated GitHub star count from jostling the nav
description: Fixes the navigation bar jitter caused by the animated GitHub star count by using CSS to set a fixed width for the star count display.
body:
The "N on GitHub" counter in the homepage nav made the nav jitter while it animated. This PR makes it hold still using only CSS:

```css
#github-stars-nav {
    min-width: 7.6em;
    font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
```

## Why it moved

- **Proportional digits.** In Geist, `2,111` renders ~12px narrower than `2,000`, so the label changed width on almost every frame of the `2,xxx` tick phase.
- **Label length changes.** The label counts up from `1` to `2,xxx`, then switches to `2.9k`.
- **Right-pinned nav.** `.landing-nav-actions` is pinned to the right edge. Each change in the label's width moved the GitHub button's left edge, and the search icon next to it moved too.

## Fix

- `tabular-nums` gives every digit the same width, so all `2,xxx` labels render at the same width (90.26px).
- `min-width: 7.6em` reserves room for the widest tick label (`2,345 on GitHub`). That covers the initial count-up and the final switch to `2.9k`, so the button never resizes. At rest the button has about 7px of extra right padding, which is hard to see.

## Verification

I recorded the real page-load animation (`1 → 2,100 → live count → 2.9k`) at 1280px wide with a MutationObserver, measuring every label update.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|

title: Detect scattered resistor-capacitor-resistor junctions
description: Detects a scattered RCR junction where two resistor paths meet a grounded capacitor, ensuring they are grouped correctly for analysis.
body:
Detect a scattered R–C–R junction: two resistor paths meet a grounded capacitor, but the three connected pins are too far apart to read as one local network. The BOOSTXL-AUDIO correction groups R32/R35/C22 around a compact junction and places C22's ground below it.

Stack: [repro #441](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/pull/441) → this solver PR. Merge the repro first.

`RcrJunctionNotGrouped` → `RcrJunctionGroupingSolver` requires exactly two resistors and one capacitor at a private three-way node, distinct resistor far-end nets, an explicitly grounded capacitor return, and matching local scope. The spacing threshold scales with symbol size. It excludes grounded divider pairs, parallel RC networks, extra junction branches and insufficient metadata; it does not infer roles from names or labels.

The complete corrected three-component extract has zero findings from the full analysis, including the pre-existing capacitor orientation warning. Component values, native symbol types and electrical connections are preserved, and visible wire continuity is tested. A separate orientation-only test confirms that rotating C22 alone leaves the grouping finding.

title: Detect resistor wire detours behind connectors
description: Detects when a resistor is placed behind its connectors connected pin, causing a wire detour around the connector body, and advises proper alignment.
body:
Extends `ResistorConnectorAlignmentSolver` / `ResistorConnectorNotAligned` to detect a resistor behind its connector's connected pin, with a visible wire detouring around the connector body. Detection uses connectivity and geometry regardless of whether either net is signal, power, ground, or has no role metadata. It does not depend on a resistor value or identifying a series/grounded branch.

Stacked on #426; merge the repro first.

![Before and after: connector resistor detour](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/refs/heads/fix/connector-ground-resistor-placement/tests/cases/__snapshots__/connector-ground-resistor-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

The corrected TSX places both CC resistors beside the connector's right-facing pins and fixes the extract's existing box-width/padding findings. The complete three-component extract reports **zero findings across all analyzers**. Native USB/resistor symbols, pin order/sides/labels, values and electrical connectivity are preserved; both CC connections are checked for continuous drawn wires. [Corrected full extract](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/fix/connector-ground-resistor-placement/tests/cases/__snapshots__/connector-ground-resistor-correction-full-extract.snap.svg); the repro retains the [complete original sheet](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/blob/fix/connector-ground-resistor-placement/tests/cases/__snapshots__/connector-ground-resistor-repro-published-sheet.snap.svg).

- Requires a two-terminal resistor, a private connector/resistor connection, valid local placement and a continuous drawn wire.
- Checks the connected pin's facing direction and whether the entire resistor body lies beyond the connector's opposite edge. The finding advises moving it beside that pin without imposing a rail-specific orientation.
- Preserves DNP/connected-NC, sheet/group, section-divider and ambiguous-connectivity guards. Unrelated connector NC pins do not suppress a valid connection.
- Retains existing facing-pin alignment behavior, including label-only connections; each pair still produces one finding.
- Tests signal/unknown and explicit power/ground roles on either terminal, zero-ohm resistors, rotations/reflections, readable placements and rejection cases. The existing programmer fixture also exercises the generic detour on a series resistor.

Real board: [seveibar/nema17-stepper-motor-driver-tmc2209-usb-pd v0.2.0](https://tscircuit.com/seveibar/nema17-stepper-motor-driver-tmc2209-usb-pd?version=0.2.0#schematic). Schematic reference: [Microchip MCP2221A USB-C Breakout Board user guide, A.2, page 24](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/APID/ProductDocuments/UserGuides/MCP2221A-USB-C-Breakout-Board-User-Guide-DS50003654.pdf#page=24). R4/R5 sit beside their CC pins with ground below; this correction follows the repro's existing pin directions.

Validation: GitHub CI passes all 332 tests, typecheck, formatting and browser build. The 9 affected local tests pass with 679 assertions. Updated snapshots were rendered and visually inspected; the corrected USB-C extract still reports zero findings across all analyzers. Timeout limits are unchanged.

Stacked on #405; merge the repro first.

Adds `ChipDiodeCapacitorNetworkNotGrouped` with `ChipDiodeCapacitorNetworkGroupingSolver`. It recognizes a typed diode and capacitor sharing a private junction with one chip, with their other terminals returning to two distinct pins on the same chip side. It reports excessive separation using symbol size and chip-pin span, without inferring function from component or pin names.

The charger correction moves D2/C7 beside U2's connected pins and keeps C5 below the local network. All four components remain visible, chip geometry and pin layout are unchanged, all electrical connections are preserved, and full analysis of the corrected extract reports zero findings.

</details>

body:
Adds `CapacitorConnectorAlignmentSolver` and `CapacitorConnectorNotAligned` for a signal capacitor whose entire body sits behind its connected connector pin. Moving it onto the pin side makes the local branch readable as a direct wire. Existing resistor/connector and chip/capacitor rules do not cover this topology.

Stack: **main → repro #396 → this solver**. Please review against the repro branch so the published fixture stays separate from the implementation.

The example is C21/JP1 from [quad-sensor-conditioner v1.0.1](https://tscircuit.com/hrithik18k/quad-sensor-conditioner?version=1.0.1#schematic). The correction preserves the header symbol/pin order, capacitance and electrical connections, and reports zero findings.

Reference: [TI THS4601 EVM, Figure 3-4, printed page 3-3 / PDF page 15](https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/slou150#page=15) draws Z3 inline with J3. This supports a visible local capacitor/connector branch; its AC-coupling function differs from this jumper-selectable filter.

The rule accepts staggered or vertical capacitors already on the pin side. It skips rails/decoupling, connector-to-connector bridges, fan-out, separate groups/sheets/sections, unpopulated parts, overlaps and incomplete geometry. Detection uses typed metadata and connectivity, without name or label heuristics.

All four matching branches are also corrected in the existing full quad-sensor fixture. Its original sheet now reports 12 findings (8 inverted grounded branches + 4 capacitor/header placements); its corrected 38-component sheet still reports **zero**. Pin-based electrical assertions accommodate generated port-ID reordering after rotation without weakening connectivity checks, and all four corrected wires are checked for visible continuity.

title: fix: prevent new trace-to-via shorts during repair
description: Repair could reduce reported DRC errors while creating a physical trace-to-via short because publication checks omitted via annuli. Check via copper across its physical drill layers, include via-to-via contacts, and invalidate prepared geometry when via diameter changes. Contact identities distinguish wire crossings from annulus contacts; same-net copper remains allowed. Preserve exact via anchors and circular pad geometry. The deferred final owner prioritizes wire crossings, tries local wire displacements and coupled moves of up to two via stacks, and validates each candidate against the whole board. It can restore affected connections while retaining independent repairs, within the existing search budgets. The portfolios early-exit heuristic remains wire-only; publication checks all copper. Reduce work and allocations in this path: prune board edges with conservative coordinate bounds, use numeric spatial-grid columns and allocate contact keys only after overlap. Native contact repair first rejects proven pad overlaps on changed or already-overlapping connections. Geometry is built only for selected owners while preserving global via ownership and numbering. Surviving proposals receive complete DRC and rejected proposals consume the original budget. Retain a bounded prefix of exact primitive geometry from the last full DRC evaluation to avoid serializing unchanged inputs. Compare coordinates, ownership, ports, widths, via dimensions and layers explicitly, including in-place mutations. Geometry shares the existing cache accounting budget with primitive keys. Engine-owned query errors are copied once at the public-result boundary, preserving caller mutation isolation. At 8ec1f3acf1c5f2b228e6f6d8c8972d4ee2045962, official standalone SRJ18(https:github.comtscircuithigh-density-repair03actionsruns42032055563) is 2.84 total time, DRC 1,079  1,078; DRC14(https:github.comtscircuithigh-density-repair03actionsruns42032060529) is -11.83, DRC 5  5. Both compare stacked base 892ddb1 on one Ubuntu runner, two basePR pairs in opposite orders, concurrency 2, Bun 1.4.4 x64. No per-case DRC increases. A separate fixed Blacksmith comparison(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouteractionsruns42031516576), using Bun 1.4.2 arm64 and copied dependencies, measures SRJ18 1.30  -1.54 and DRC14 -11.49  -12.18 against the same stacked base. Against the previous published repair 6ec16dc, isolated cases 6 and 13 are 10.2113.35 and 7.4810.44 faster with identical output hashes. Case 13 memory is mixed. Full-pipeline measurements, including all slower repeats and identical-main memory controls, are in the consumer PR(https:github.comtscircuittscircuit-autorouterpull3496). All 186 repair tests pass (50,526 assertions) and both TypeScript projects pass. Tests cover 3,606 exhaustive board-distance pairs, 3,200 spatial-order oracle cases, obstacle-filter parity, duplicate-via ownership, mutation isolation, cache eviction and bounded geometry reuse. Consumer integration passes six tests  637 assertions and typecheck. Hosted CI is green; the branch is conflict-free. Stacked on 189; merge 189 first. The six-route output gap becomes 0.05572 mm instead of -0.06523 mm; the real Game Boy replay retains 0.08638 mm clearance instead of publishing -0.00107 mm overlap.
body:
Repair could reduce reported DRC errors while creating a physical trace-to-via short because publication checks omitted via annuli. Check via copper across its physical drill layers, include via-to-via contacts, and invalidate prepared geometry when via diameter changes. Contact identities distinguish wire crossings from annulus contacts; same-net copper remains allowed. Preserve exact via anchors and circular pad geometry.

The deferred final owner prioritizes wire crossings, tries local wire displacements and coupled moves of up to two via stacks, and validates each candidate against the whole board. It can restore affected connections while retaining independent repairs, within the existing search budgets. The portfolio's early-exit heuristic remains wire-only; publication checks all copper.

Reduce work and allocations in this path: prune board edges with conservative coordinate bounds, use numeric spatial-grid columns and allocate contact keys only after overlap. Native contact repair first rejects proven pad overlaps on changed or already-overlapping connections. Geometry is built only for selected owners while preserving global via ownership and numbering. Surviving proposals receive complete DRC and rejected proposals consume the original budget.

Retain a bounded prefix of exact primitive geometry from the last full DRC evaluation to avoid serializing unchanged inputs. Compare coordinates, ownership, ports, widths, via dimensions and layers explicitly, including in-place mutations. Geometry shares the existing cache accounting budget with primitive keys. Engine-owned query errors are copied once at the public-result boundary, preserving caller mutation isolation.

At `8ec1f3acf1c5f2b228e6f6d8c8972d4ee2045962`, [official standalone SRJ18](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/actions/runs/42032055563) is +2.84% total time, DRC 1,079 → 1,078; [DRC14](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/actions/runs/42032060529) is -11.83%, DRC 5 → 5. Both compare stacked base `892ddb1` on one Ubuntu runner, two base/PR pairs in opposite orders, concurrency 2, Bun 1.4.4 x64. No per-case DRC increases.

A [separate fixed Blacksmith comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/42031516576), using Bun 1.4.2 arm64 and copied dependencies, measures SRJ18 +1.30% / -1.54% and DRC14 -11.49% / -12.18% against the same stacked base. Against the previous published repair `6ec16dc`, isolated cases 6 and 13 are 10.21–13.35% and 7.48–10.44% faster with identical output hashes. Case 13 memory is mixed. Full-pipeline measurements, including all slower repeats and identical-main memory controls, are in the [consumer PR](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3496).

All 186 repair tests pass (50,526 assertions) and both TypeScript projects pass. Tests cover 3,606 exhaustive board-distance pairs, 3,200 spatial-order oracle cases, obstacle-filter parity, duplicate-via ownership, mutation isolation, cache eviction and bounded geometry reuse. Consumer integration passes six tests / 637 assertions and typecheck. Hosted CI is green; the branch is conflict-free.

Stacked on #189; merge #189 first. The six-route output gap becomes +0.05572 mm instead of -0.06523 mm; the real Game Boy replay retains +0.08638 mm clearance instead of publishing -0.00107 mm overlap.

title: perf: reuse broad-force passes and avoid redundant DRC work
description: Reduces redundant DRC evaluations by reusing broad-force passes and optimizing candidate evaluations in the autorouting process.
body:
Repeated native force proposals paid for identical DRC evaluations, and rejected 12-pass broad attempts replayed the same first 12 passes when trying 24 passes. Coarse spatial-grid candidates also triggered exact projections for pairs whose live bounds were already farther apart than the required clearance.

Reuse the broad-pass prefix while the incumbent is unchanged, detach returned geometry before extending it, and restart after accepting a new incumbent. Reject distant pairs with conservative live bounds before exact contact calculations. Keep logical candidate counts, pass budgets, acceptance checks, contact tie behavior, and custom-evaluator calls unchanged. The native regression retains **six logical attempts while reducing DRC evaluations from eight to four**.

Current head `483187739f20e4268ce4feabb2aada8976304c73` is stacked on [repro #186](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/186), with current repair main's correctness fixes preserved. Both this PR and [consumer #3368](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3368) are conflict-free. The consumer pins this exact head.

Validation: **165 tests / 41,347 assertions** and typecheck pass locally; repair CI tests, typecheck, and format pass. The consumer's **7 focused tests / 678 assertions** and all **9 CI test shards** pass, alongside its other checks.

Official `/benchmark --same-machine --dataset ...` comments were posted as **techmannih**, using `dataset01`, `18`, `33`, and `24`. All requested full datasets have completed. The benchmark keeps the existing effort, concurrency, timeouts, DRC checks, and memory measurement.

| Dataset / full round | Runtime P50 | Runtime P95 | Memory P50 | Memory P80 | Memory P90 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41911866555) | +0.83% | -5.04% | -2.46% | +0.08% | -0.81% |
| [SRJ18 round 1](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41911368147) | -0.08% | +1.07% | -0.43% | +10.27% | +2.31% |
| [SRJ18 round 2](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41913816088) | +2.48% | +0.30% | -1.53% | -2.60% | -0.12% |
| [SRJ18 round 3](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41913813904) | +0.17% | -1.36% | -0.80% | -5.57% | -2.28% |
| [SRJ24](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41911867708) | +2.43% | +0.00% | -2.03% | +1.07% | -3.29% |
| [SRJ33](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41911857916) | -1.44% | -0.64% | +1.07% | +4.16% | -3.67% |

The screenshot's **+8.8% was Memory P80**, not runtime. It came from SRJ18 `sample014`. Three predefined current full-cohort rounds measure **+10.27%, -2.60%, -5.57%** at Memory P80 (median **-2.60%**); `sample014` occupies P80 in every round. These observations do not support a stable +8.8% increase, but the unfavorable first round remains included. Three isolated repeats were +4.00%, -2.13%, +0.04%; those single-sample runs do not replace the full-cohort comparisons. A universal zero-increase memory/runtime gate is not established.

The original reviewed SRJ33 ordinal 32 is `sample051`. The current full benchmark measures **29.737 → 28.238 seconds (-5.04%)**; global repair **2.595 → 1.321 seconds (-49.09%)**. Routing outcomes are unchanged.

Across the four full datasets, all **164 board outcomes** are unchanged, including completion, timeout status, DRC counts/types, vias, and trace-lint counts. SRJ24's existing failures/timeouts remain in the report; its timeout-penalized P95 is not a successful-board tail measurement.

Provenance: base consumer `41673fb0cd159303cc68796e9fe4d04692b92a8e`; first full rounds use consumer `079d7f2`, while the two SRJ18 repeats and isolated checks use current `9b5a12b`. Those consumer heads differ only in the repair pin: old `e62f85a` and current `4831877` have the **identical complete Git tree** `32db0d94ef183c04972bf9c6fe4194f58ae3fd97`. Bun 1.4.2, Blacksmith ARM, three concurrent samples, one routing thread, effort 1, 360-second sample timeout.

Older [controlled performance measurements](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41689685997) used earlier frozen revisions and remain historical evidence, separate from the current results above.

Additional diagnostics also retain unfavorable results. [Two opposite-order ablation rounds](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41913426200) measured base/fix peaks of 2118/2061 MiB in round 1 and 2055/3256 MiB in round 2; disabling duplicate checks also produced a 3134 MiB peak. The initial timer hook only recorded start/end because inline routing blocked the timer.

A [follow-up with direct stage-boundary recording](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41916229436) measured base/fix peaks of 2015/2062 MiB and 2020/3130 MiB. In its large-gap round, current RSS was already **1770 vs 2824 MiB before global repair**, and **1789 vs 2844 MiB after global repair**. The gap appeared during port-point pathing/high-density routing, before the changed force-candidate paths ran. Thus the large observed gap is not evidence that the resumable broad-force runner itself retained that extra GiB. All diagnostic routing outcomes remain unchanged. These instrumented, isolated runs are separate from the official full-cohort table.

The precise allocator/GC cause remains unconfirmed, and intermittent RSS spikes are **not claimed fixed**. The latest pushed update reconciles the stack and dependency pin. No additional memory-specific algorithm change was made.

title: test: reproduce duplicate native DRC work across force scales
description: Adds a regression test to reproduce duplicate native DRC evaluations across different force scales without changing production code.
body:
A three-point trace with a fixed endpoint inside a foreign pad produces identical rejected geometry at three force scales. This passing regression records the current cost explicitly: `expect(nativeEvaluationCount).toBe(8)`. There is no `test.failing` marker.

The same fixture also checks successful solver completion, unchanged input/output routes, one existing DRC issue, and six logical candidate attempts. [Fix #187](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/187) changes the exact assertion from `8` to `4`, so the reduction is directly visible in its diff while the output-quality assertions stay unchanged. This is a native evaluation count, not a claim of a 50% full-board speedup.

No production code changes. Based on repair main `28d833001e903ff5ba1342694762ef2a56555cad`. The focused repro passes locally at `714b4ba`; the fix's full 156-test suite also passes.

Earlier diagnostics on autorouter `6f7d91e` showed SRJ18 sample009 performing 36 snapshot evaluations for 18 unique geometries. Samples002/009/015 already finish through initial bounded regional repair, so this repro does not assume the historical later regional-search path still occurs.

title: Honor circular pad geometry in repair DRC and forces
description: Fixes DRC evaluation and repulsion for circular SMT pads by treating them correctly as circles instead of rectangles, leading to a reduction in DRC findings.
body:
Repair treated declared circular SMT pads as rectangles in both DRC evaluation and repulsion. Preserve their circular outline so repair can use valid diagonal gaps.

The real OrangeCrab DDR board keeps all 50 nets connected and drops from 28 physical DRC findings (including two shorts) to zero. The nRF control keeps its original DRC counts.

[Before/after SVGs and consumer PR](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3487) · [Repro](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3486)

title: fix: preserve existing plated-hole transitions in repair DRC
description: Fixes the issue where existing plated-hole transitions were converted into new vias, ensuring that these transitions are preserved during the repair DRC process.
body:
Repair DRC converted an existing `through_obstacle` layer transition into a new via. With via-in-pad disabled, repair then moved the connection outside its plated hole.

Preserve that marker when converting HD routes. Unmarked layer changes still produce vias and retain the pad-drill check.

Required by tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3473.

title: Fix own-net pad drills in the existing repair solver
description: Fixes the issue where repair skips connected pads and trades away cleared drills while improving copper clearance when an SRJ disallows vias in pads.
body:
When an SRJ disallows vias in pads, repair still skips connected pads and can trade away a cleared drill while improving copper clearance.

Score the drill separately from connected copper, repair it first using the measured overlap, and reject candidates that increase forbidden drills. This uses the existing repair search; no additional solver or routing pass.

Alternative to the repair04 approach in tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3470, which remains open. Real OrangeCrab integration and before/after SVGs: tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3471.

title: batch power trace expansion while preserving work budgets
description: Reduces the routing time of the powerTraceExpansionSolver from around 20 seconds to 1.5 seconds by batching operations and adjusting iteration budgets.
body:
When checking the timing of each solver powerTraceExpansionSolver only gets around 20s for routing, that is now reduced to 1.5s which is around 12x speedup.

autorouter link https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3442

title: fix: use the published altiumts package
description: Updates the dependency from a Git checkout to the published altiumts package version 0.0.95, ensuring proper installation and functionality without lifecycle trust exceptions.
body:
The converter pins a Git checkout of altiumts whose package exports point at missing dist files during an ordinary downstream install. Standalone currently works around that with a root dependency override.

Use published altiumts ^0.0.95, which includes its built entrypoints, and remove the Git lifecycle trust exception. Consumers can install and bundle the converter normally.

Validation: TypeScript check passes; all 206 tests pass after downloading the repository's reference fixtures. The repository-wide format check reports existing differences in documentation and its schema version; this change preserves the manifest's existing formatting.

title: Define seated JST PH/SH plug and contact profiles
description: Defines the seated insertion depth, narrow plug nose, and SH contact-row offset in the shared PHSH dimensional profile for better compatibility between core and jscad-electronics.
body:
Cable plugs currently start at a header's outer lip, leaving their contacts disconnected. Define the seated insertion depth, narrow plug nose and SH contact-row offset in the shared PH/SH dimensional profile so core and jscad-electronics can use the same physical interface.

These are representative mating envelopes with clearance for the modeled sockets. The existing `matingDepth` continues to locate the outer lip; the seated plug tip is `matingDepth - plugInsertionDepth`. No model strings or user props change.

Validation: 311 tests passed; typecheck, format check and build passed. Paired geometry: https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/515
Paired endpoint/origin fix: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5115
Regenerated docs: https://github.com/tscircuit/docs/pull/981

Merge/release this dimensional contract first, followed by the renderer; core and docs are draft until the released dependencies can be updated.

title: perf: prune clearance pairs and simplify via-pad distances
description: Reduces computational overhead by pruning clearance pairs and simplifying distance calculations for point-shaped vias while maintaining exact geometry and projection order.
body:
Clearance projection repeatedly enumerated distant segment pairs and used a general segment-distance routine for point-shaped vias. This PR removes that work while retaining exact geometry and projection order.

### Concrete changes

- [Pair preparation](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/blob/57763abb9b086c0a556499b806a95cb6e371435b/lib/RelaxTraceClearanceSolver.ts#L327): spatially query nearby segment bounds instead of enumerating every pair. Across the 13 existing real repros, prepared candidates fall **10,068,159 → 675,670 (-93.3%)**.
- [Query results](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/blob/57763abb9b086c0a556499b806a95cb6e371435b/lib/RelaxTraceClearanceSolver.ts#L380): reject already-visited indices inside Flatbush's query before allocating/sorting them. The retained indices still run in their original ascending order.
- [Via-pad distance](https://github.com/tscircuit/repair04/blob/57763abb9b086c0a556499b806a95cb6e371435b/lib/obstacleDistanceGeometry.ts#L52): for an exact point input and rectangular pad, compute distance to its coordinate-wise clamp using the existing `math-utils` helpers. This is the same distance already present in the general routine, without its redundant edge intersections and corner comparisons.

The per-segment bounds cache was removed after it slowed dense moving geometry. `projectPair` and `projectPad` now use the baseline's direct bounds arithmetic. Exact narrow-phase predicates, clearance thresholds, displacement limits, all 256 sweeps, physical guards, acceptance rules and search budgets remain unchanged.

### Measured result

Baseline `0b3bf0f` / pinned `88504e8` source versus production code `57763ab`; Apple M4, Bun 1.3.14:

| Measurement | Base | PR | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Projection total, five-run median over all 13 real repros | 605.344ms | 409.029ms | **-32.4%** |
| Previously slower dense sample14 tangent case | 167.678ms | 157.783ms | -5.9% |
| Captured sample015 joint DRC, three-run median | 9.590s | 6.792s | **-29.2%** |
| Full SRJ18 joint DRC, all 16 boards | 35.354s | 28.171s | **-20.3%** |

Every public projection-case median is faster (-5.9% to -62.4%). Every full-suite joint DRC stage is faster (-3.9% to -33.9%). Routes remain byte-identical.

</details>

### Benchmark method

The local measurements used the 13 existing real repro fixtures and unchanged legacy geometry SHA manifest. Five baseline/PR pairs ran in alternating fresh processes. Only solver construction and solve were timed; input parsing, route hashing and printing were outside the interval. Every output was checked against its legacy hash. The complete per-case medians and raw total times are recorded above.

### Correctness and limits

- All 13 immutable geometry hashes and all 11 captured projection outputs are unchanged; captured inputs remain unmodified.
- The point/reference test passes **11,325 exact comparisons**, including pad boundaries, zero-sized pads, signed zero, large translations and extreme finite scales. No tolerance was added.
- Focused source type checking passes locally. Four local SVG snapshot mismatches also occur on the baseline; their assertions and snapshots were left intact. The preceding point-distance revision passes all 186 CI tests / 614337 assertions; CI results are tracked in the PR checks.
- Full SRJ18 integration solves 16/16 with zero DRC issues/timeouts, unchanged vias/lint and byte-identical route SVGs. The captured joint replay keeps 465 attempts, 164221 search nodes and 12 top-level reference validations.
- Whole-routing total/P50/P95 are roughly 0.4–0.5% slower in this local pair, so this PR claims the measured projection/DRC improvement, not a demonstrated overall routing speedup. Fresh matched integration CI comparisons are queued in https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3477, whose diff remains a single dependency pin.

title: fix: connect shared DDR RAM and test-point branches
description: Fixes routing issues by connecting shared DDR RAM and test-point branches to ensure all endpoints are preserved and connected correctly.
body:
Shared DDR nets with a third RAM or test-point terminal stop at the fanout solver's two-terminal guard. Route between the main packages first, then attach extra terminals to existing same-net copper using the same router. Preserve every endpoint and all supplied copper.

Stacked on #150. The **same real ButterStick repro now connects 8/8 signals and all 24 endpoints**, with native copper DRC passing. A separate native TSX/core run connects **16/16 i.MX6 data signals**, including the DATA8 test point, with zero findings in eight physical checks. The full i.MX6 request now connects **53/53 signals**, but has **138 reported physical findings**; it is not DRC-clean.

The fix changes two production files and the existing SVG. The repro test and captured input are unchanged.

| Before: third terminal rejected | After: both RAM packages connected |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/86c691174b633d6b3a0af46733e1b80e43b33e07/tests/repros/__snapshots__/butterstick-shared-ddr.snap.svg) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/a6c55202b5e2321e57edf0807577ef8a387be57b/tests/repros/__snapshots__/butterstick-shared-ddr.snap.svg) |

| Board | Initial result / full goal | Latest verified progress |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H616 | 0/53 signals | 8/8 DQ subset clean; combined bytes still fail. |
| ButterStick | 0/55 signals | **8/8 shared DQ signals**, all 24 endpoints connected, zero physical findings in native TSX/core output. The two-byte request still reaches the 120-second limit. |
| Glider | 0/49 signals | 16/16 DQ subset clean; remaining signals still fail. |
| i.MX6 | 0/53 signals | **53/53 signals connected**; 138 physical findings remain. Separate **16/16 DQ-only** request is clean, including TP27. |
| iCE/Pi | 0/50 signals | 16/16 DQ subset clean; remaining signals still fail. |

Subset runs are separate committed requests, not completed boards. This adds connectivity for unconstrained multi-terminal nets; timing-constrained trees still fail explicitly rather than treating branch lengths as bus skew.

Native core rendering exposed two additional failures at `bf1bd6e` that the earlier solver-only validator missed: tuning on `EMI0_CK_T` and `EMI1_DQS0_T` touched its own via land. Pinned-bus pair tuning now uses the terminal-via guard and checks the joined result again. Small fixtures preserve both rejected approaches, and regressions agree with core's self-short checker. The full retained copper and overview are replaced by the corrected, accepted result; existing native strategies keep their previous tuning options. ### Reproduction and validation - Fresh native core render at solver revision `220b7949bbdef8e4d58fec539cd6da12bb6a582e`: **138/138 accepted**, all 18 bus constraints and 12 pair/coupling checks pass, no invalid geometry, terminal-via approaches or via-in-pad holes. Core reports no circuit errors. The export audit verifies each physical trace and plated via against accepted solver copper. - Core render and checks: **791.35 seconds** with the default routing budget; independent validation ran afterward. Bun 1.4.4, Linux x64, 2 GiB JSC heap hint. This is not a controlled performance comparison. - Original input SHA-256: `be7707c9188ba888fc551fcc341b424eefdb5c65e2ab9e593c3a9829b1fe4221`. Accepted SRJ: `34ecb9dc4ba22b9cf6cb8c17fe63b18e56da1e0daff1d81bc7780591edb490a6`. Circuit JSON: `4211deedc11e6ecaa408abfab2cdd9b0b6524cde6e6e936a9fde28dc9fa4a097`. - Targeted fresh pair/byte routing, native-pair behavior, input constraints, via regressions, retained snapshots and board-export tests pass. Export regressions reject missing/duplicate traces, changed copper and moved drill holes. Typecheck, formatting, build and isolated Node/browser/TypeScript package consumers pass. - The saved full-board images were independently revalidated, rendered and visually inspected. Retained-output tests are separate from the fresh core solve. Artifact commit `375ca9df3f8a31f7634fe2bb506c712488ec57a7` has the same library tree as `220b794`. The pinned published core bundles an older solver. The end-to-end harness substitutes only that dependency binding in memory using a guarded Bun loader; it retains core's native adapter, SRJ construction, render lifecycle, circuit checks and export. It does not use `algorithmFn` or change solver options. The published package alone does not yet contain this fix. See the [repro instructions](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/tree/375ca9df3f8a31f7634fe2bb506c712488ec57a7/repros/mt8395-lpddr4x). ```sh bun install (cd repros/mt8395-lpddr4x/source && bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts) BUN_JSC_forceRAMSize=2147483648 BUN_JSC_miniVMHeapGrowthFactor=1.05 \ bun repros/mt8395-lpddr4x/source/route.tsx full bun repros/mt8395-lpddr4x/board-export.ts full ``` This completes the DDR routing research fixture. Power, reference planes, decoupling, boot circuitry and hardware SI qualification remain outside its scope. ### AM3352 benchmark effect **Final-revision Blacksmith comparison passed: 11/11 → 11/11**, with no lost completions, failures or timeouts. Both revisions passed 47/47 connectivity, DRC, bus/pair matching, coupling/geometry quality and fixed-copper preservation on every sample. Input hashes and reported skews agree. Timings are mixed: P50 76.069 → 58.912 s (−22.6%), P90 612.712 → 533.177 s (−13.0%), P95 716.283 → 718.257 s (+0.3%). Observed regressions include `outer-layers` 612.712 → 903.337 s (+47.4%), `left` 20.810 → 32.192 s (+54.7%), and `inner-layers` 52.291 → 58.912 s (+12.7%). No uniform speedup is claimed. The via guard is enabled for pinned native buses; existing native strategies retain their tuning options. The final head and pinned base/controller revisions are listed in the comparison below. Both used identical fixtures, harness and 3,600-second per-solver/sample budgets, Bun 1.4.0 on Blacksmith 4-vCPU Linux runners, with dependency installation before timing. For each of the 11 entries in `scripts/pr-benchmark/samples.json`, CI ran `bun base/scripts/pr-benchmark/run-pair.ts --sample --timeout-seconds 3600 --main base/lib/index.ts --pr head/lib/index.ts --main-sha --pr-sha --controller-sha --output results/.json`. This launches the same fresh worker entry point as `./benchmark.sh`; saved routes are not counted as solves. Raw reports and the analysis are retained in the linked workflow artifacts.

title: Add MT8395 LPDDR4X repro from exact core inputs with visual snapshot
description: Adds a reproducible MT8395AVZA LPDDR4X routing case using the exact SimpleRouteJson emitted by cores built-in bus_lanes phase. Includes independent full-board (138 signals), byte-zero (11), and DQS-pair (2) captures, all retaining 1,446 pads. The replay loads this checkouts solver without adding global layers or modifying geometry, ownership, matching constraints, or via permissions. The repro includes pinned TSX recapture tooling, input hashes and signal names, baseline measurements, and a visual input snapshot. The snapshot labels dashed connections as unrouted airwires, refuses suppliedpartial copper, and has a narrowly scoped AGENTS exception for this requested diagnostic. Accepted output still requires complete connectivity, DRC, buspair matching, coupling, and an ownership-independent via-in-pad check.
body:
Adds a reproducible MT8395AV/ZA LPDDR4X routing case using the exact SimpleRouteJson emitted by core's built-in `bus_lanes` phase. Includes independent full-board (138 signals), byte-zero (11), and DQS-pair (2) captures, all retaining 1,446 pads. The replay loads this checkout's solver without adding global layers or modifying geometry, ownership, matching constraints, or via permissions. The repro includes pinned TSX recapture tooling, input hashes and signal names, baseline measurements, and a [visual input snapshot](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/blob/5513886ae9734415a72cd469fe36c61d5358308a/repros/mt8395-lpddr4x/board.snap.svg). The snapshot labels dashed connections as **unrouted airwires**, refuses supplied/partial copper, and has a narrowly scoped AGENTS exception for this requested diagnostic. Accepted output still requires complete connectivity, DRC, bus/pair matching, coupling, and an ownership-independent via-in-pad check. ![MT8395 exact core input — unrouted requests, not completed copper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/5513886ae9734415a72cd469fe36c61d5358308a/repros/mt8395-lpddr4x/board.snap.svg) ### Input audit and fresh repro results Fresh captures with `tscircuit@0.0.3057` / `core@0.0.2252` match the earlier experimental inputs exactly. No core fix is warranted: endpoints, circular obstacles, bus layers, pair constraints, widths, clearances, and disabled via-in-pad are preserved. The redundant-global-layer workaround is intentionally absent. | Exact core input | Fresh source-solver result | | --- | --- | | DQS pair, 30 s budget | Tuning-clearance failure after 5.36 s | | Byte zero, 60 s budget | Routing timeout; 0 accepted routes | | Full board, 60 s budget | Routing timeout; 0 accepted routes | These bounded failures do not prove unroutability. This is a routing research fixture; power/reference copper and hardware qualification are absent. ### Validation - `bun run typecheck` and the standalone repro tsconfig: passed. - `bun test tests/mt8395-core-input.test.ts`: 3 passed. - Repository-wide Biome formatting check and `git diff --check`: passed. - Snapshot rendered and visually inspected. - Baseline: `005bee4ae0af17cea30108e4f57d58cd4b2dc430`; head: `5513886ae9734415a72cd469fe36c61d5358308a`; Bun 1.4.4, Linux x64. ### Benchmark effect **Final-revision Blacksmith comparison passed: 11/11 → 11/11**, with no lost completions, failures or timeouts. Both revisions passed 47/47 connectivity, DRC, bus/pair matching, coupling/geometry quality and fixed-copper preservation on every sample. Input hashes and reported skews agree. This repro leaves the library tree identical to base `3cac3bc`. Measured timing varies despite identical solver code: P50 76.384 → 82.707 s (+8.3%), P90 847.989 → 718.182 s (−15.3%); `control-inner1` increased from 847.989 to 1198.655 s (+41.4%). These are measurements from this paired run, not evidence of an algorithmic speedup or slowdown. The final head and pinned base/controller revisions are listed in the comparison below. Both used identical fixtures, harness and 3,600-second per-solver/sample budgets, Bun 1.4.0 on Blacksmith 4-vCPU Linux runners, with dependency installation before timing. For each of the 11 entries in `scripts/pr-benchmark/samples.json`, CI ran `bun base/scripts/pr-benchmark/run-pair.ts --sample --timeout-seconds 3600 --main base/lib/index.ts --pr head/lib/index.ts --main-sha --pr-sha --controller-sha --output results/.json`. This launches the same fresh worker entry point as `./benchmark.sh`; saved routes are not counted as solves. Raw reports and the analysis are retained in the linked workflow artifacts.

title: Route A64’s fourth DDR byte through available pad-edge escape sites
description: Adds drill-clear positions beside round pads and broadens blocked site domains for A64s fourth data byte routing, enabling connection of all data lines with zero physical findings.
body:
A64’s fourth data byte had no usable assignment among the sampled BGA-grid escape sites. Add drill-clear positions beside round pads and broaden blocked site domains after the original search fails. Extra positions are opt-in for this DDR retry, preserving the established routing paths.

The real TSX/core data-only run now connects **32/32 data lines with zero physical findings**, versus 24 completed lines before. All 24 earlier routes are identical. The full 75-signal section still times out on its remaining 43 signals.

Stacked on #146. [SVG before/after](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/147/files). **562 tests pass**, as do typecheck and formatting. The complete fresh local benchmark passes **11/11 on both revisions with identical outputs**; the required Blacksmith acceptance job also reports **11/11 passed**.

title: repro: A64 fourth DDR byte fails after 24 completed routes
description: Reproduces a failure in routing the last eight data lines of the A64 TSX circuit after successfully routing the first 24, capturing the cores exact input and adding a failing SVG regression without changing production solver behavior.
body:
The real A64 TSX circuit routes its first 24 data lines, then rejects the last eight. This captures core’s exact input and adds a deliberately failing SVG regression; only the previously completed copper is shown.

[Real TSX repro and provenance](repros/a64-byte3/README.md). No production solver or AM3352 inputs change. title: Negotiate blocked DDR escape sites instead of freezing pad-layer fallbacks
description: Preserves successful allocations while allowing negotiation of generated signal sites when routing fails due to blocked DDR copper.
body:
Earlier DDR copper can block nearby via sites. Later signals fall back to the pad layer, and routing stalls while keeping those generated choices fixed.

Keep successful allocations. After a bounded failed attempt, reuse the existing site/layer negotiation and geometry finish while preserving supplied copper.

Stacked on #140. Both captured phases now connect all eight new signals with zero DRC findings. The SVG changes are visible in Files changed; failed baselines stay in the repro PR.

title: Fix STMP157 DDR byte routing with valid pad-to-via approaches
description: Fixes routing issues for STMP157 DDR byte connections by implementing valid pad-to-via approaches, ensuring all connections pass DRC checks.
body:
Stacked on #137. The repro owns the unchanged real-board input, test and failed SVG; this PR changes only the solver and that same snapshot.

The three pad-to-via stubs on DQ26, DQ27 and DQ30 were non-axis/45° wires. Reuse the existing normalizer on those native-layer approaches, preserving terminals, via positions and the 24 supplied traces. The unchanged repro now passes all eight connections and DRC checks.

| Before: repro #137, failed candidate copper | After: completed 8/8 new signals |
| --- | --- |

Local test, types and formatting pass. The earlier full validation passed 558 tests and **11/11 → 11/11 AM3352 comparisons**, with identical iterations, DRC, lengths, skew and coupling measurements. Both production `lib/` trees are byte-for-byte identical to that measured comparison; only the repro/snapshot layout changed. Fresh CI for the new stack SHAs is running and remains required before merge.

The TSX/core data-only rerun connected all 32 data signals cleanly with all 710 pads unchanged. The full 72-net run still hits 6 GiB in the remaining-signal stage; timing closure is untested.

title: Add idle holding to stepper jog controls
description: Releasing a stepper jog currently drops coil current as soon as braking finishes. The gantry and single-motor pages now have a Hold position when idle checkbox. With it enabled, an axis retains its final coil phase after a jog or saved-position GOTO. Each gantry axis can hold independently. The native stepper firmware reports holding separately from movement and keeps the existing stop and protection paths active. The browser continues heartbeats while holding and releases on Stop, focus loss, or disabling the checkbox. The checkbox is off by default and requires compatible firmware. Validated with native host tests, browser controller tests, and Pico SDK builds for DRV8825, DRV8847, DRV8452, and A4988. Physical holding torque and temperature have not been measured.
body:
Releasing a stepper jog currently drops coil current as soon as braking finishes. The gantry and single-motor pages now have a **Hold position when idle** checkbox. With it enabled, an axis retains its final coil phase after a jog or saved-position GOTO. Each gantry axis can hold independently.

The native stepper firmware reports holding separately from movement and keeps the existing stop and protection paths active. The browser continues heartbeats while holding and releases on Stop, focus loss, or disabling the checkbox. The checkbox is off by default and requires compatible firmware.

Validated with native host tests, browser controller tests, and Pico SDK builds for DRV8825, DRV8847, DRV8452, and A4988. Physical holding torque and temperature have not been measured.
