title: Allow custom installation destinations without administrator access
description: Enables users to select writable installation destinations without requiring administrator privileges, enhancing installation flexibility across Windows, macOS, and Linux.
body:
The Windows installer hides its destination page, while the Unix installers default to locations that can require administrator access. This change lets users choose writable destinations and keeps installation within their existing permissions.

- Windows: show the destination page, retain `PrivilegesRequired=lowest`, add PowerShell `-Destination` support, and recheck command conflicts after folder selection.
- macOS: offer a portable destination in the terminal and a custom prefix in the package wizard. Keep the default `~/.local` installation separate from the optional folder choice so Installer resolves it inside the current user's home. Remove the `sudo` installation path.
- Linux: prompt for a prefix, default to `~/.local`, preserve managed upgrades and portable installs, and fail on unwritable paths without escalating.
- Update generated release instructions and macOS CI/release checks to use the per-user installation.

Checksum/signature verification and existing-command consent remain in place. Unix users can run the printed absolute command or add their chosen `bin` directory to PATH.

Validation: [CI passed](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/42099726849) on `a591477`: typechecking and the regression suite, all five builds, both native macOS installs without administrator access, and the Windows bootstrap and installer lifecycle. The manual signing job was skipped as expected. Also verified both macOS destinations locally with an isolated package fixture.

title: fix: allow bundled native modules in signed macOS releases
description: Fixes the failure of notarized macOS ARM binaries to load bundled native modules due to ad-hoc signing without a Team ID, by adding necessary entitlements and improving CI dependency installation and synchronization processes.
body:
The notarized `daily-2026-11-05` macOS ARM binary fails before `tsci --version` with `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED`: the hardened executable has tscircuit's Team ID, while its bundled `resvgjs.darwin-arm64.node` is ad-hoc signed without a Team ID.

Add `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` to the release entitlements so the executable can load its bundled native modules. Developer ID signing, hardened runtime, timestamping, and notarization stay in place. Both macOS release architectures now run a post-install smoke script with a fresh HOME/cache, a system-only PATH, and external networking denied. It checks version/help, initializes a project with bundled dependencies, builds the LED example through the embedded worker and native PNG renderer, verifies output files, and imports RP2040.

The PR also fixes failures exposed by full CI qualification:

- Dependency installation: legacy `sharp@0.32.6` inherits Node's five-second HTTPS socket timeout. GitHub release redirects exceeded that limit; a local reproduction failed at 5.2 seconds with the default agent and received HTTP 302 at 6.8 seconds with an explicit timeout. Give CI installs a 60-second socket timeout, preserving TLS validation and explicit request timeouts. Retry recognized download failures up to three times, removing partial node_modules between attempts while preserving package caches. Persistent failures retain a nonzero exit code; other install errors stop immediately. Selected-release preparation uses the same wrapper.
- Browser setup: download the pinned Playwright Chromium browser using the hosted runner's existing shared libraries, avoiding unrelated OS font collections that stalled at the Ubuntu mirror. All offline browser checks remain enabled.
- Offline import synchronization: retry individual request timeouts while waiting for both imported files, keeping a fixed 60-second overall deadline. Fail immediately if dev exits or the endpoint returns HTTP errors or malformed data.
- Windows installer qualification: poll the launched process with a monotonic deadline and progress messages, preserve its exit code under Windows PowerShell 5.1, read redirected output while detached descendants retain writer handles, and terminate timed-out process trees. Launch test processes in separate hidden consoles. Silent CI installs/upgrades pass `/NOCLOSEAPPLICATIONS /NORESTARTAPPLICATIONS` so Restart Manager cannot close or restart the test host; the installer defaults for users are unchanged.

Validation:
- [Full CI run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/42051365238) passed on `72a7d2cb33c5f8329c3a91988ed42d241f1a81e8` on its first attempt: all 11 active jobs succeeded, including macOS ARM/Intel verification, Windows install/upgrade/uninstall/rollback, and the offline 3D board/STEP model check. The optional manual Windows-signing job was skipped as expected.
- Original downloaded macOS ARM binary: the new offline smoke script reproduces the native-library Team ID failure.
- Separate copy locally re-signed with the updated entitlements: all offline smoke stages pass.
- Fresh installation of `sharp@0.32.6` with the CI timeout fix: succeeds and renders a native PNG.
- Three local HTTPS regression tests: slow redirects, explicit shorter timeouts, and rejection of untrusted certificates. Passed with external networking denied on Bun 1.3.14 and CI's Bun 1.4.4.
- Four dependency-install fixtures: clean retry with caches preserved, exhaustion after three attempts, immediate failure for other errors, and selected-release preparation.
- Seven import synchronization regressions, including bounded timeout handling and error propagation.
- Windows process fixtures pass under both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.
- Local signing/release tests, strict TypeScript checks of the new helpers/tests, shell syntax, plist linting, and `git diff --check` pass.

A new Developer ID-signed release was not produced locally. The release workflow runs the macOS smoke check against the installed, notarized package before publication.

title: Include system block viewer in standalone browser dependencies
description: Adds the system block viewer as a dependency in the standalone browser to resolve missing-module errors during runtime.
body:
The [0.0.3082 release](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/41866894315/job/126703346244) fails while inspecting RunFrame's browser imports: RunFrame 0.0.3141 imports `@tscircuit/system-block-viewer`, which is listed only in its development dependencies. Standalone explicitly supplies RunFrame's UI dependencies, but its pinned list did not include this new viewer.

Add the same versioned `0.0.2` tarball used by RunFrame to the UI workspace and record its integrity and dependency graph in `bun.lock`.

Validation with Bun 1.4.4 and the exact failed release, `tscircuit@0.0.3082`:
- Reproduced the missing-module error from a clean checkout; browser preparation now produces all 11 entrypoints and 8 assets.
- [Release qualification](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/41868369968): backend/UI type checks and the complete suite pass (227 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed); all five binary artifacts build successfully.
- Linux qualification passes offline init/install/add with zero external connection attempts, all 914 baked datasheets, and 3D STEP rendering and WASM at dev and nested static-site URLs with external networking disabled.
- Local macOS native compilation, version check, offline package installation, and browser/STEP checks pass. The browser check required a rerun after a 3D-tab click timeout.

The initial CI datasheet request timed out; rerunning preparation passed. Windows installer verification is being retried after its five functional native-cache tests passed but temporary-directory cleanup failed with `EBUSY`.

title: Fix dependency resolution for standalone release builds
description: Fixes dependency resolution issues for standalone release builds by declaring the schematic trace solver and native GLTF converter directly, aligning runtime dependencies with the selected npm releases requirements, and ensuring proper compilation and regression coverage checks.
body:
The daily release of `tscircuit@0.0.3075` [fails while preparing browser modules](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/41813465333). RunFrame's nested Core imports an undeclared schematic trace solver, which was previously supplied by an unrelated transitive dependency. After fixing that first failure, native compilation also exposes older root dependencies and a UI adapter substituting a converter that lacks the selected Core's mesh-loading API.

Declare the schematic trace solver and native GLTF converter directly. During release preparation, align overlapping root runtime dependencies with the selected npm release's requirements, retaining compatible pins and the reviewed CLI/UI packages. Resolve the release schema in browser bundles and their evaluation worker, and limit the GLTF substitution to the STEP exporter it was intended to adapt.

Regression coverage checks release dependency alignment, preservation of CLI/UI pins, invalid metadata, and compilation of a consumer requiring GLTF exports absent from the UI converter.

Validation with Bun 1.4.4 and the failed release version `0.0.3075`:
- Reproduced the original failure from a clean frozen installation, then repeated that installation with the complete fix.
- Browser modules, baked datasheets, native dependency cache, native macOS binary, and prototype UI/evaluation worker build successfully.
- Backend/UI type checks and all 13 focused tests pass.
- The compiled executable reports `0.0.3075`; native init/install/add and uncached-package rejection smoke checks pass with an empty package-manager PATH.
- [Release qualification](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/41846327286) and [normal PR CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/41846273983) both pass backend/UI type checks and the full regression suite: 227 passed, 4 platform/artifact-dependent skips, 0 failures. All five binary targets, the Linux browser checks with external networking blocked, and native macOS checks pass. The remaining Windows installer smoke timeout also occurs on [unchanged main](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/41746496107/job/126303501649), before this PR. That installer issue is being investigated separately.

title: Use an explicit embedded Bun runtime for offline standalone installs
description: Standalone uses its embedded Bun 1.4.4 runtime and a prepared native package cache for offline tsci init and tsci install, ensuring no external connections are made during these operations.
body:
Standalone uses its embedded Bun 1.4.4 runtime and a prepared native package cache for offline `tsci init` and `tsci install`. It pins `@tscircuit/cli@0.1.2430`, which includes the runtime selection support from merged [CLI PR #5671](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5671).

**Offline Docker demo (2:15)**

[![Watch the offline Docker CLI recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/7964e376fe745877c37858e19150ff83dd594955/docs/demos/tscircuit-offline-docker-preview.png)](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/raw/7964e376fe745877c37858e19150ff83dd594955/docs/demos/tscircuit-offline-docker.mp4)

[Watch/download the MP4](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/raw/7964e376fe745877c37858e19150ff83dd594955/docs/demos/tscircuit-offline-docker.mp4) · [Raw recording, traces, and reproduction scripts](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/raw/7964e376fe745877c37858e19150ff83dd594955/docs/demos/tscircuit-offline-evidence.zip)

Recorded with Docker `--network none`, a failed internet probe, and an initially empty cache. Shows init, reinstall, add/remove, uncached package/tarball/Git rejection, and circuit build. All ten CLI invocations recorded **zero external connection/send attempts**; the system Bun checksum and PATH stayed unchanged. Long idle pauses are shortened; command output, including starter design/catalog warnings, is retained.

The shared CLI invokes `TSCIRCUIT_NODE_RUNTIME` directly with child-only `BUN_BE_BUN=1`. Standalone supplies a temporary native bunfig through `TSCIRCUIT_NODE_RUNTIME_ARGS`, selecting the restored cache with `install.offline = true` and `install.ignoreScripts = true`. This leaves the user's PATH and system Bun unchanged. Bun handles dependency resolution, installation, lockfiles and offline misses.

The cache includes init requirements, the selected runtime release, and optional packages for all target OS/CPU combinations. Files and manifests retain their native contents; metadata preserves executable modes and portable index links. First invocation restores the cache, and later invocations reuse it. Build inputs retain seed lockfiles and cached package notices. The captured `latest` tag is the preparation-time registry snapshot.

Validation:

- CLI build, TypeScript check, and 14 focused runtime/entrypoint/init tests passed.
- Standalone compilation, type checks and full local suite passed against the published CLI release: 226 passed, 4 skipped.
- Compiled init, reinstall, add, and uncached package/tarball/Git rejection passed with no package manager on PATH. Network tracing recorded zero non-loopback connection/send attempts.
- Cache fixtures verify unchanged PATH/user agent, script suppression and config precedence over a project bunfig that enables networking.
- Compiled build/site/dev and Chromium qualification passed, including 914 baked datasheets, browser modules, WASM exporters, 3D board and STEP rendering.

CI qualification against the published CLI release passed: all five target builds, Linux network-isolated install/browser tests, native macOS ARM64/x64 tests, Windows offline installs, and Windows installer install/upgrade/rollback/uninstall checks. The Windows job passed on a fresh-runner retry after the first runner stopped responding beyond its step timeout and did not upload logs. No code changes or checks were bypassed for the retry.

The existing `altiumts@0.0.59` override and bundled autorouter runtime keep compiled builds working with the pinned toolchain. Separately invoked system package managers and arbitrary user code are outside the offline install policy.

See [implementation notes](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/blob/codex/standalone-offline-dependencies/docs/offline-dependencies.md) for cache lifecycle and native configuration.

title: straightened-stages: derive wire-stage returns from pcb_stackup (stripline gets both planes)
description: Fixes the inability to model a stripline between two ground planes by allowing wire-stage returns to be derived from the PCB stackup, enabling correct modeling of return paths for stages without explicit profiles.
body:
Fixes #50. `straightened-stages` needed a hand-written `straightened_stage_profiles` entry for every layer, and each entry allowed only one return bar. So a stripline between two ground planes (AM3352 DQS on `inner2`, with GND on `inner1` and `inner3`) couldn't be modelled correctly. ## Before / after This PR changes one box in the pipeline, highlighted below. Everything else, including the `routed-copper` fork, is unchanged. **Before** ```mermaid flowchart TD A["TSX → @tscircuit/core → circuit JSON"] --> B["validateCircuitRecords"] --> C["modelingFromCircuitJson
requires straightened_stage_profiles"] --> D["route lookup + stage list"] D --> F{"reduction?"} F -- routed-copper --> A1["routedCopperGeometry"] --> A2["groundMesh"] --> A3["copper decks"] F -- straightened-stages --> B1["stage cells"] --> B2["CHANGED: profile → 1 return box
hand-written, one plane only"]:::changed --> B3["fastHenryDeck / fasterCapDeck"] A3 --> S["solve twice + check"] B3 --> S S --> I["ibis-to-spice"] --> N["channel.cir → ngspice"] --> E(["eye diagram + results.html"]) classDef changed fill:transparent,stroke:#e5534b,stroke-width:4px ``` **After** ```mermaid flowchart TD A["TSX → @tscircuit/core → circuit JSON"] --> B["validateCircuitRecords"] --> C["modelingFromCircuitJson
NEW: profiles optional"]:::changed --> D["route lookup + stage list"] D --> F{"reduction?"} F -- routed-copper --> A1["routedCopperGeometry"] --> A2["groundMesh"] --> A3["copper decks"] F -- straightened-stages --> B1["stage cells"] --> B2{"NEW: profile for
this layer?"}:::changed B2 -- yes --> P["1 return box from profile
(as before)"]:::changed B2 -- "no · wire stage" --> G["NEW: return from pcb_stackup + GND pours
1 box per adjacent plane
stripline → 2 boxes, one conductor"]:::changed B2 -- "no · via stage" --> X["NEW: error, via needs a profile"]:::changed P --> B3["fastHenryDeck / fasterCapDeck
NEW: multi-part return"]:::changed G --> B3 A3 --> S["solve twice + check"] B3 --> S S --> I["ibis-to-spice"] --> N["channel.cir → ngspice"] --> E(["eye diagram + results.html"]) classDef changed fill:transparent,stroke:#2da44e,stroke-width:4px ``` ## Change When a wire stage's layer has no profile, its return comes from the board: - **Planes:** each directly adjacent copper layer that carries a pour on the reference ground net, reached from `channelReference` (`src/stage-returns.ts`). - **One 2 mm return bar per plane**, with height, thickness and εr from `pcb_stackup`. A stripline gets both planes. - **The bars form one `return` conductor:** - parallel `parts`, joined with `.equiv` at both ends in the FastHenry deck, with one `.external`; - one FasterCap conductor; - the DC analytic check sums the part areas. - **Lane spacing** is the median routed centre-to-centre distance when no profile declares it. - **Declared profiles still win.** Via stages still need an explicit `via` profile; the error now says so. - **No layer with ground next to it:** explicit `return_geometry` error asking for a profile. No props, core or circuit-json changes: `straightened_stage_profiles` is already optional there. Only the pipeline's own "profiles required" check is removed. ## Verification - **New `tests/stage-returns.test.mjs`:** - a derived microstrip return; - an explicit error when there's no adjacent ground plane; - stripline returns in both planes; - both decks treat the parts as one conductor. - **`pnpm typecheck`:** clean. - **`pnpm test`:** 173 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (pre-existing). - **Real board, AM3352 DQ0 on `top`** ([board PR](https://github.com/0hmX/am3352-ddr-track-a-local-dfm-wip-20261007/pull/9)): with the hand profile removed, the derived geometry is identical to the hand-written one (2 mm × 0.0152 mm bar, 0.1245 mm below, εr 4.1). title: Release to GitHub instead of npm
description: Changes the release process to create GitHub release assets instead of publishing to npm, addressing the issue of the package not being available on npm.
body:
## Why
`@tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline` isn't on npm, and the workflow's token can't create it. Every "Publish to npm" run on `main` pushed a version tag and then failed:

```
npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@tscircuit%2fpcb-spice-pipeline
```

That left tags `v0.1.4`–`v0.1.6` with no package. Releases have been made by hand as GitHub release assets (`v0.1.3`, `v0.1.6`), and that's what tscircuit/cli depends on:
`https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/releases/download/v<version>/tscircuit-pcb-spice-pipeline-<version>.tgz`

## Change
`.github/workflows/pnpm-pver-release.yml`, renamed "Release":
- Same checks as before: typecheck, test, test:package.
- `pver release --git --package-json` bumps the version in the tag commit and pushes the tag. It doesn't publish to npm or push to `main`.
- The script checks out the newest `v*` tag, verifies `package.json` has the same version, runs `npm pack` (which builds), and runs `gh release create <tag> <tgz> --verify-tag --generate-notes`.
- If the tag already has a release (a rerun, or a `[norelease]` commit), it skips.
- Permissions are reduced to `contents: write`. `id-token` and `pull-requests` aren't needed any more, and neither is the npm token.

This takes a different approach from #27 (a `package-releases` branch served through jsDelivr), and both edit the same workflow file. Merging this one means closing #27.

## Validation
- `actionlint` 1.7.12 reports no issues for the release and CI workflows.
- I ran the release script in a scratch clone of `main`:
  - With real `gh`: `Release v0.1.6 already exists; nothing to publish.`
  - With `gh` stubbed so no release exists: it checks out `v0.1.6`, the version matches, it packs `tscircuit-pcb-spice-pipeline-0.1.6.tgz`, and it calls `gh release create v0.1.6 … --verify-tag --title v0.1.6 --generate-notes`.
  - The packed tarball's SHA-256 (`989c75f7…`) is identical to the manually published `v0.1.6` release asset.

title: Grade ring edges already split by the T-junction repair
description: Fixes TypeError during copper extraction by ensuring boundary grading handles existing edge pieces correctly after T-junction repair.
body:
## Problem
After #33–#39, the AM3352 run gets through routed-copper extraction and circuit-node construction. It then crashes while building the FasterCap deck:

```
TypeError: Spread syntax requires ...iterable not be null or undefined
    at splitEdge → meshPolygon → face → surfacePanels → copperFasterCapDeck → extractChannel
```

The failing polygon is a ground-pour island: a via-clearance arc whose apex (vertex 6) lies **exactly** on the island's outer edge 16→17 (x = −1.649946, t = 0.5).
1. `meshPolygon`'s T-junction repair correctly splits edge 16→17 at vertex 6.
2. Boundary grading then still calls `splitEdge(16, 17, …)` on the original edge, which no longer exists in `edgeTris`.

## Change
- Boundary grading walks the **existing pieces** of each ring edge: the edge itself, or the ordered chain of collinear vertices the repair inserted. Each graded point goes into the piece it falls in, and points that coincide with a piece endpoint are skipped.
- If a piece is genuinely missing, it fails with a `ground_geometry` diagnostic instead of a `TypeError`.
- Edges that were not split behave exactly as before.
- `meshPolygon` is exported so it can be tested directly, like `groundMesh` and `panelAspectLimit`.

## Tests
- New `tests/copper.test.ts` case uses the exact 19-vertex AM3352 ring captured from the failing run. It meshes at panel sizes 0.2, 0.02 and 0.005 mm, and the triangle area matches the ring's shoelace area to 1e-9. It fails before this change with the `TypeError`.
- `pnpm test`: 161 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.

title: Cut channel nets that are split into per-subcircuit records
description: Fixes routing failure by cutting channel nets that are split into per-subcircuit records, ensuring proper handling of net bindings across subcircuits.
body:
## Problem
After #33/#35/#36/#37/#38, the AM3352 run gets through routed-copper extraction and then fails while building the circuit nodes:

```
channel_short: Extracted endpoints are shorted by another ideal source trace or reference
```

`circuitNodes` cuts the redundant one-port-to-net bindings of a two-terminal channel only when **both endpoints bind the same `source_net`**. Subcircuits scope net records, so on the AM3352 board the logical `DDR_D0` is three records:

```
CPU pin  --source_trace_255--> DDR_D0@Processor --source_trace_2743 (net-only)--> DDR_D0@board
RAM pin  --source_trace_591--> DDR_D0@DDR3      --source_trace_2831 (net-only)--> DDR_D0@board
```

The endpoints never bind the same net id, so nothing is cut. The union then joins CPU and RAM pins through the board-level net.

## Change
- Group net records joined by **net-only** traces (non-channel traces with no ports).
- Compare endpoint bindings by group, and apply the existing cut to every record in the group.
- The safety checks apply to the whole group:
  - `channel_short` if any record is ground;
  - `channel_net` if a trace links the group to an outside net or a port binds several nets;
  - `channel_fanout` if any other port binds into the group.
- A single shared net is a group of one, so the existing behavior is unchanged.

## Tests
- New `tests/general.test.mjs` case: the straight fixture with `DQ@cpu`/`DQ@ram`/`DQ@board` records arranged as above. The endpoints get distinct nodes and the board record is cut. Adding a third port tap on `DQ@board` still fails as `channel_fanout`. It fails before this change with `channel_short`.
- `pnpm test`: 161 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.

title: Treat same-named per-subcircuit ground net records as one ground
description: Fixes ground net ambiguity by treating same-named per-subcircuit ground net records as a single ground, resolving extraction errors in subcircuits.
body:
## Problem
Subcircuits scope `source_net` records, so a board-wide `GND` appears once per subcircuit, with the records joined by traces. On the AM3352 board, the CPU ground ball `U1.A1` reaches **12** `GND` records (`Processor`, `DDR3`, …, and the board subcircuit). After the bridge and schema fixes (#33, #35, #36), routed-copper extraction stops with:

```
ground_net: The channel reference must connect to exactly one source_net marked is_ground
```

No board with subcircuits can meet that requirement. `routedCopperGeometry` already collects pours and vias across **every** connected net (`netIds`). The single `net` was only used for the report's `sourceNetId`/`sourceNetName` and an error message.

## Change
- Use one ground when the reference connects to several `is_ground` records that **all share one name**.
- Name it after the record the reference pin's own trace connects to.
- Differently named grounds shorted together (for example `AGND`/`DGND`) are still rejected as ambiguous.

The existing `ambiguous` case in `tests/copper.test.ts` keeps failing as before.

## Tests
- New `tests/copper.test.ts` case: the ground-plane fixture plus a same-named `GND` record in another subcircuit, tied through the receiver ground pin. Extraction succeeds, is named after the reference pin's own record, and uses the same pours. It fails before this change with `ground_net`.
- `pnpm test`: 161 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.

title: Accept saved core pcb_group and board-text records in schema validation
description: Fixes schema validation errors for saved core pcb_group and pcb_silkscreen_text records by handling null values and formatting numeric display offsets correctly.
body:
## Problem
After the bridge fixes (#33, #35), `tsci simulate` on the AM3352 board stops at schema validation, before any extraction:

```
circuit_schema: pcb_group pcb_group_0: anchor_alignment: Expected 'top_left' | … , received null
circuit_schema: pcb_silkscreen_text pcb_silkscreen_text_246: pcb_component_id: Required
```

On that board, core output fails circuit-json validation in these places:

| Record | Field | Count | Saved value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pcb_group` | `anchor_alignment` | 74 | `null` |
| `pcb_group` | `display_offset_x/y` | 7 | number |
| `pcb_silkscreen_text` | `pcb_component_id` | 20 | `null` (board-level text) |
| `pcb_component` | `display_offset_x/y` | 347 | number (already aliased here) |

The `pcb_silkscreen_text` override (`z.string().nullable()`) also *requires* the key. So the form current circuit-json specifies ("omitted for board- or group-level text") is rejected too.

## Change
Use the existing `compatible(...)` helper, which validates a normalized copy and returns the original record:
- `pcb_group`: drop `anchor_alignment: null` and format numeric display offsets as `"<n>mm"` before validation.
- `pcb_silkscreen_text`: drop `pcb_component_id: null` before validation, so both `null` and an omitted key validate.
- Numeric display-offset handling is shared with the existing `pcb_component` alias.

Saved records are never rewritten. Invalid values such as an unknown anchor or a numeric `pcb_component_id` are still rejected.

Core is also being fixed to stop emitting these forms. This PR keeps boards that were already saved working.

## Tests
- New `tests/circuit-schema.test.mjs` case covers both the legacy (`null`/numeric) and the circuit-json (`"center"`/string/omitted) forms of each field. It checks that records are left unchanged and that invalid values are still rejected. It fails before this change.
- `pnpm test`: 161 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.

title: Accept board-level reference vias in pads of nested-subcircuit parts
description: Allows board-level vias in pads of nested subcircuit parts to be recognized as direct contacts for routed-copper extraction, resolving issues with ground connections.
body:
**Stacked on #35** (uses its `subcircuitTree`). Retarget to `main` after #35 merges.

## Problem
After #33/#35/#36/#37, routed-copper extraction on the AM3352 board stops at the CPU ground reference:

```
ground_connection: source_port_334: require one routed ground lead to a reference via/pour
```

`U1.A1` has a via-in-pad (`pcb_via_230`, top→inner1, barrel inside the inner1 `GND` pour). The via is board-level (`subcircuit_source_group_74`), but the pad belongs to `U1` inside the `Processor` subcircuit (`subcircuit_source_group_0`). Direct pad/via contacts required `via.subcircuit_id === port.subcircuit_id`, so the via was discarded. The code then looked for a routed lead, and A1 doesn't have one.

## Change
Accept a direct-contact via whose subcircuit **contains** the pad's subcircuit (`subcircuitTree(circuit).within(port, via)`). The physical checks are unchanged:
- barrel inside the pad;
- trace or net connected to the pin;
- span and plating;
- barrel inside ground copper.

A via owned by a nested subcircuit still can't serve a pad outside it.

## Tests
- New `tests/via-in-pad.test.ts` case: the via-in-pad fixture with both parts' pads moved into a child subcircuit, so the vias are board-level. Both reference contacts resolve to the via (contact radius 0.15 mm). The reverse case (vias nested, pads at board level) is still rejected with `ground_connection`. It fails before this change.
- `pnpm test`: 164 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.

title: Scope channels across sibling subcircuits to their common subcircuit
description: Fixes simulation failures caused by cross-subcircuit channels in sibling subcircuits by implementing a common subcircuit scoping mechanism.
body:
## Problem
A DDR write channel runs from the processor to the memory, and boards often keep those in sibling subcircuits under the board subcircuit. The AM3352 board does (`Processor` and `DDR3`). After the round-trip fix in #33, `tsci simulate` on that board fails with:

```
tsx_scope: BYTE0_WRITE_QUIET: selected pins cross saved subcircuits
```

Scopes were compared by exact innermost subcircuit:
- `serializeSimulation` rejected experiments, probes and nets whose pins sat in different subcircuits.
- Plan building in `declarations.ts` only accepted models, channel endpoints and probes in exactly the experiment's subcircuit.

So any cross-subcircuit channel was impossible.

## Change
- New `src/subcircuit-scope.ts` builds the saved subcircuit tree from `source_group` parentage. It provides `within(inner, outer)` and `common(scopes)` (nearest common subcircuit, with `undefined` as the unscoped root).
- `tsx-render.ts`:
  - Experiment scope = common subcircuit of its IBIS pin states.
  - Probe scope = common subcircuit of its signal and reference terminals.
  - Unscoped net scope = common subcircuit of its pins. An explicit `net.subcircuit_id` must still contain all its pins.
- `declarations.ts`: models, channel endpoints and probes are accepted when they are **contained in** the experiment scope.

Still strict: without an explicit experiment scope, models in several unrelated subcircuits are still rejected ("multiple modeled subcircuits require an explicit experiment scope"). Pins in unrelated top-level subcircuits only share the unscoped root.

## Tests
- `tests/subcircuit-scope.test.ts`: containment and nearest-common-ancestor cases, including an intermediate non-subcircuit group and unrelated roots.
- `tests/tsx.test.ts`: a driver and a receiver in sibling `CPU`/`RAM` subcircuits round-trip through `ImportedBoard`. The experiment is scoped to the board subcircuit, a RAM-local probe to `RAM`, and a CPU→RAM probe to the board. It fails before this change with `selected pins cross saved subcircuits`.
- `pnpm test`: 163 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.
- AM3352: with #33 and this change, `serializeSimulation` succeeds on the real board. The run then stops on core emitting schema-invalid records (`pcb_group.anchor_alignment: null`), which is being fixed in core separately.

title: Make ImportedBoard internal to this package

It isn't how tsci projects should simulate: they already author their boards in TSX and can put the declarations directly in their own `<board>`.

When a tsci project used it anyway (the AM3352 DDR board), two things went wrong:

- Mark `ImportedBoard` `@internal` and document that it isn't supported in tsci projects.
- README: replace the "TSX bridge" section with "Simulating a board", which says to declare models, transient experiments, stimuli, probes and eyes as children of `<board>`.

title: Pre-mesh routed copper into well-shaped FasterCap panels
description: Fixes ill-conditioning in FasterCaps collocation system by pre-shaping routed copper panels, improving solver performance and accuracy.
body:
Fixes #28.

## Problem
The routed-copper FasterCap deck sent the solver huge, extremely thin panels:
- each 12.6 × 2.6 mm pour face as two sliver triangles, with a minimum angle of about 0.03°;
- 12.6 mm × 8 µm pour side walls;
- 10 mm × 35 µm trace walls.

The collocation system was badly conditioned. GMRES needed 470–1000+ iterations, C swung from 0.94 to 1.54 pF depending on `capacitanceTolerance`, and only 0.08 passed the reciprocity check. Even then C was 31% too low.

FasterCap flags alone can't fix this. Under `-a`, FasterCap ignores `-t`. Jacobi, two-level and Galerkin preconditioners, and fixed `-m` meshes all still stall or swing by ±30%.

## Fix
When `copperFasterCapDeck` gets extraction settings, as it does on the pipeline's routed-copper path, `surfacePanels` now pre-shapes the copper:
- **Faces** use a graded constrained-Delaunay mesh. Panel size is half the signal width at the signal and grows by 0.5 × distance, up to the existing `maxPanelLength`.
- **Side walls** are split so no panel is longer than 10 × the copper thickness.
- **An earcut T-junction** left by collinear via-hole edges is split at the vertex on it.

The closed copper solid and the area-preservation check are unchanged. No new user settings.

## Results (issue geometry, deck built by this branch's `copperFasterCapDeck`, pipeline flags `-a<tol> -ap -e`)
Reference C is 1.378 ± 0.003 pF. Two independent non-FasterCap dense-LU BEM solvers agree on it, and the 2D per-length value matches Hammerstad/Wheeler thick-strip formulas to within 0.2%.

| tolerance | before | after | GMRES iters (before → after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | ✗ reciprocity 0.065 | ✓ 1.367 pF (−0.8%) | 473 → 11 |
| 0.08 | ✓ 0.953 pF (−31%) | ✓ 1.367 pF (−0.8%) | 723 → 11 |
| 0.05 | ✗ GMRES 1000-iter fail, 115 s | ✓ 1.361 pF (−1.2%) | 1000 → 12 |
| 0.03 | — | ✓ 1.335 pF (−3.2%) | → 16 |
| 0.02 | ✗ > 40 min | ✓ 1.340 pF (−2.8%) | → 18 |

Every FasterCap run finishes in under 0.4 s. The deck grows from 236 to about 9k input panels.

## Alternatives tried
- **Solver flags only:** no combination passes at every tolerance.
- **Modeling thin copper as zero-thickness sheets:** this fixes the conditioning, but C stays 5–12% off unless the panels are also well shaped. It could be an opt-in follow-up on top of this change.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 160 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped. Adds a test that checks graded faces, wall aspect ratio, `maxPanelLength` and an unchanged closed-solid volume.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- Not yet run: a full `tsci simulate` of the issue repro against this branch. The results above come from a reconstruction of the issue geometry run through `copperFasterCapDeck`.

title: Hide and isolate the board in pre-rendered GLBs
description: Fixes the issue where boards in GLB mode could not be hidden or isolated due to missing identifiers, enabling proper visibility controls for board components.
body:
Follow-up to #1091. That PR made the board hideable and isolatable when the viewer renders Circuit JSON, but in GLB mode (`CadViewer glbUrl` / `glbData`) the exported board nodes carried no id. The board then disappeared only when something else was isolated. tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#285 now tags the board, its "Via Plating" and stiffener nodes with `extras.tscircuit.pcb_board_id` (a panel's `pcb_panel_id`).

### Changes
- `prepareGlbScene` / `getGlbComponentMetadata` copy `pcb_board_id` into `userData`. The existing `pickSceneObject` branch then returns `Hide "Board"` / `Isolate "Board"` for GLB boards.
- `GlbScene`'s `applyVisibility` treats `pcb_board_id` as an object id, the way it treats `cad_component_id`. The textured board loads as a group of meshes, so hiding the group hides all of them. Boards in older GLBs carry no id and keep the previous behavior.
- `stories/assets/prerendered-glb/fidget-counter.glb` is regenerated from its published Circuit JSON and models with the #285 exporter. Its binary chunk and every other JSON field are byte-identical to the previous fixture. Only `Box0` and `Via Plating` gain `pcb_board_id: "pcb_board_0"`. The README has the new size and SHA-256.
- New 18.6 KB fixture `tests/assets/prerendered-board.glb` (textured board, via plating, one part), built by `scripts/generate-prerendered-board-glb.ts`. A new test in `tests/object-visibility-scene.test.tsx` loads it, picks the board and the part, then hides and isolates the board. It fails without the `src` change.

### Verification
- `bun test`: 238 pass, 0 fail. The biome format check is clean.
- Prerendered GLB → Fidget Counter story, in headless Chromium: after hiding the cap and X1, right-clicking the board offers Hide/Isolate "Board", and Isolate leaves only the board.
- `tsc --noEmit` reports one error in `tests/section-glb-url.test.tsx` (`fetch.preconnect`). Clean `main` with the same `node_modules` shows the same error, so it isn't from this PR.

### Follow-up
The `circuit-json-to-gltf` devDependency (0.0.143, used only by the renderer-comparison script and the new generator script) still needs bumping once #285 is released. The committed fixtures already carry the board extras, so tests pass without the bump.

The runner records phase/solver timings, render RSS, physical connectivity, routing check findings, native pad geometry, and partial SRJ artifacts. Every circuit uses a fresh process with an external timeout; incomplete or failed routing cannot count as a passing board. PR code runs with read-only permissions, and a separate job posts the report.

title: Honor the configured catalog proxy for all search providers
description: Routes search calls for JLCPCB, TI, DigiKey, Mouser, and KiCad through the configured catalog proxy instead of using raw fetch calls, ensuring proper proxy usage for all search providers.
body:
With a local catalog proxy configured, JLCPCB, TI, DigiKey, Mouser and KiCad search still used raw fetch calls and could bypass the proxy. Route those calls through the existing `getPlatformFetch()` interface, as registry and datasheet search already do.

Datasheet search uses `TSCIRCUIT_DATASHEET_API_BASE_URL` when supplied, including any path prefix, and uses the normal registry endpoint when it is unset. Deployments can select datasheets by default using the existing `TSCIRCUIT_DEFAULT_SEARCH_SOURCES`. `TSCIRCUIT_BAKED_ASSET_SERVER_DIR` already starts the local file server and supplies its provider URLs.

```sh
TSCIRCUIT_DATASHEET_API_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000/catalog/datasheet-api \
TSCIRCUIT_DEFAULT_SEARCH_SOURCES=datasheets tsci search RP2040
```

There are no new transports, environment variables, standalone checks, or file readers in the search command. Missing configured responses do not fall back to public catalogs.

Validation: 33 focused tests passed, covering configured and unset datasheet URLs, path prefixes, empty and unavailable catalogs, loopback-only search, mocked normal searches, imports, and the existing file server. Typecheck, full Biome formatting check, and CLI build passed. The proxy subprocess test exits immediately if a request targets anything other than its configured local server.

title: fix: avoid exhaustive surface-site search for untimed A13 buses
description: Avoids exhaustive surface-site search for untimed A13 buses by attempting ordinary lane routing first, retaining surface-site search on the first retry for timing-constrained buses.
body:
A13’s CPU data buses have no timing constraints, but exhaust surface-site search before ordinary lane routing connects them.

Try ordinary lane routing first for untimed buses. Keep surface-site search on the first retry, and retain the existing strategy for timing-constrained buses. Stacked on #158.

| Real A13 CPU-side bytes | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fresh TSX/Core solve | 122.82 s | 5.42 s |
| Solver steps | 1,276,307 | 4,283 |
| Connected signals | 16/16 | 16/16 |
| Physical findings | 0 | 0 |

The input, all 378 pad primitives and completed copper are byte-identical. Top and bottom remain allowed. This improves CPU-to-resistor routing time; the full A13 interface still times out.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/30779b4c28df50335b6db99d7824374398ecc0fe/tests/__snapshots__/a13-cpu-bytes-pcb.snap.svg) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/32f6e664dec5c19436fbb0eecb3ce305a7043451/tests/__snapshots__/a13-cpu-bytes-pcb.snap.svg) |

The SVG caption records solver steps; the copper stays identical.

Readability cleanup `a17486d`: nine focused routing tests, formatting and typecheck pass; the A13 SVG and solver-step count are unchanged. Latest revision: [full CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/42279746898) and [11-case benchmark](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/42279746826).

The recorded timings and complete-suite results are for `32f6e66`: 583 tests passed locally and in CI, all 23 DDR cases retained their previous copper and findings, and 17 clean cases were preserved.

<details><summary>Completed 11-case benchmark comparison</summary>

[Fix benchmark: 11/11 accepted](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/42273189003). The [repro-only baseline also freshly accepts 11/11](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/42272901164). There are no lost completions. Each accepted case has 47/47 signals, zero native DRC findings, full-copper bus skew within 0.635 mm, pair skew within 0.127 mm, valid coupling and all 161 fixed power traces preserved.

Pinned base/controller: `30779b4c28df50335b6db99d7824374398ecc0fe`; head: `32f6e664dec5c19436fbb0eecb3ce305a7043451`. Blacksmith 4-vCPU Ubuntu 24.04, Bun 1.4.0; 3,600 seconds per solver/sample; fresh sequential processes with identical fixtures and budgets. The base controller runs `scripts/pr-benchmark/run-pair.ts --sample <sample> --timeout-seconds 3600 --main base/lib/index.ts --pr head/lib/index.ts`, which invokes `scripts/benchmark.ts`, the same entry point as `./benchmark.sh`.

[Full paired report, including exact solver durations and measured per-bus/pair skew](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/42273189003/artifacts/13534265343).

title: Reuse large copper-pour triangulations across PCB presets
description: Reuse the triangulation of large copper pours across scene changes, optimizing performance and memory usage during rendering.
body:
Reuse the triangulation of large copper pours across scene changes. The per-drawer cache checks every vertex and hole offset and retains at most 24 MiB of typed arrays. Release the full CPU mesh after upload.

Measured with PCB Viewer and the preloaded TMDS62LEVM Full and Minimal assets from demo commit `aac0ff2`. Two fresh Chrome sessions per revision, each with five Full → Minimal → Full cycles. Warm frame times are medians. Peak RSS is summed across the Chrome processes for each session.

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full frame | 3,017 ms | 1,934 ms |
| Minimal frame | 2,108 ms | 1,335 ms |
| Full compile and upload | 2,314 ms | 1,304 ms |
| Minimal compile and upload | 1,626 ms | 841 ms |
| Peak Chrome RSS | 3,684–3,733 MiB | 3,575–3,640 MiB |

No asset refetches during switching. The two presets produced byte-identical vertex and index buffers, and the returning Full board screenshot matched pixel for pixel. The regression covers two different pours with the same lookup key and eviction under the byte limit. The SK-AM62 Full and Without Connectivity pair now reuses both pours. The Without Multimedia and Without Expansion pair needs about 26 MiB for all cacheable pours and can still miss at the 24 MiB limit. Both pairs produced meshes identical to uncached rendering.

The local Chrome visual suite stops at the existing AM3352 snapshot mismatch. Main and this branch produced identical actual and diff PNGs for that case.

title: Preserve via anchors when blocked path sampling advances
description: Fixes the omission of entering-layer endpoints of through vias in RVboys path simplifier when blocked path sampling advances, ensuring all vias are retained across layer transitions.
body:
RVboy's path simplifier could omit the entering-layer endpoint of a through via. When a blocked minimum-size step crossed the via, it clamped the vertex index but advanced the path distance if the leaving-layer vertex was already appended. Subsequent copper started 0.243 mm away on the other layer, and crossing-via reduction threw.

Clamp the path distance at the detected layer transition as well. The exact captured route retains all eight vias instead of seven, with matching XY coordinates across each layer transition.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Missing via and disconnected trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/trace-simplification-solver/codex/rvboy-simplifier-via-anchor/tests/solvers/__snapshots__/rvboy-via-anchor.before.png) | ![Preserved via connects both layer anchors](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/trace-simplification-solver/codex/rvboy-simplifier-via-anchor/tests/solvers/__snapshots__/rvboy-via-anchor.snap.png) |

The repro runs the exact full captured input: one target route, 584 surrounding routes, 1,016 obstacles and the original connectivity map. SHA-256 provenance is checked. Only the drawing is cropped to x = −19.2…−17.8 mm, y = 2.5…3.9 mm. Gray copper belongs to surrounding routes. This snapshot demonstrates via continuity, not whole-board clearance.

Validation: 59 tests pass (14,050 assertions), TypeScript and formatting pass. The original code reproduces the mismatched layer transition at (-18.445, 3.089) → (-18.536943, 3.313440). Both snapshots were visually inspected. RVboy's separate full-board clearance failures remain under investigation.

title: Limit route removal to occupied spatial buckets
description: Limits route removal to only those spatial buckets that are occupied by the route, significantly improving performance during copper removal operations.
body:
Track the occupied buckets for each route when the spatial index first needs to remove copper. Subsequent replacements visit only those buckets and preserve other routes in the same buckets.

- On the saved `srj18` sample 2 via-cleanup input, median cumulative removal time fell from 45.3 ms to 2.6 ms over 12 alternating pairs. All 244 output routes matched exactly.
- On the captured sample 12 simplification input, median stage time fell from 1.73 s to 1.05 s over eight alternating pairs. All 504 output routes matched exactly.
- All 58 tests passed, including shared buckets, multiple routes with the same name, and re-adding a removed via. TypeScript passed.

Full-board comparison in [tscircuit-autorouter #3541](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3541).

title: Search bundled datasheets through the existing local file server
description: Upgrades tscircuitcli from 0.1.2438 to 0.1.2444 and sets the default search source to the bundled datasheet catalog, ensuring search requests are handled locally without external networking.
body:
Upgrade `@tscircuit/cli` from `0.1.2438` to published version `0.1.2444`, which includes tscircuit/cli#5723, and default standalone search to the bundled datasheet catalog.

The runtime change sets `TSCIRCUIT_DEFAULT_SEARCH_SOURCES=datasheets`. The existing `TSCIRCUIT_BAKED_ASSET_SERVER_DIR` setup supplies the local file-server URLs. Search requests, including explicit source flags and missing responses, remain on that server.

The compiled smoke checks cover catalog hits, misses, source overrides, and non-loopback traffic. The trace parser recognizes connected loopback TCP sends reported by `strace -yy`; regression tests cover the original Linux failure and rejection of external destinations.

Validation: standalone and UI typechecks, 255 passing tests, and the compiled Linux search/install and browser checks with public networking disabled. The network trace reports zero non-loopback connection/send attempts, including cache misses.

title: Restructure into domain modules and rename to signal-integrity-pipeline
description: Splits the flat src into 11 modules grouped by what each one owns. Output is byte-identical to main. Design and rationale: docsARCHITECTURE.md(..blobrestructuredomain-modulesdocsARCHITECTURE.md).
body:
Splits the flat `src/` into 11 modules grouped by what each one owns. Output is **byte-identical to `main`**. Design and rationale: [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../blob/restructure/domain-modules/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). ## What the library does, and who owns each step Workflow (the same diagram is now in the README): ```mermaid flowchart TD board[/"Your board
(Circuit JSON)"/] --> s1["1. Read the board, pick the wires to study
board"] chips[/"Chip models
(IBIS files)"/] --> s3 s1 --> s2["2. Measure the wires: R, L, C
extraction"] s2 <-->|"runSolver"| fs{{"FastHenry + FasterCap"}} s1 --> s3["3. Build one circuit: wires + chips
buffers, simulation"] s2 --> s3 s3 --> s4["4. Simulate the signals over time
simulation"] s4 <-->|"runSolver"| ng{{"ngspice"}} s4 --> s5["5. Judge signal quality: eyes, DDR timing
observation, ddr"] s5 --> out[/"Results + report
(HTML, CSV)"/] ``` ## How `runPipeline` runs now State machine: the seven typed stages, grouped into three phases. No solver runs before `bound`, and the compiler enforces that. ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 state "Check (no programs run yet)" as check { direction LR [*] --> input input --> admitted: read board admitted --> declared: plan work declared --> bound: prepare chip models } state "Run programs" as solve { direction LR [*] --> extracted: measure wires extracted --> simulated: simulate signals } state "Finish" as finish { direction LR [*] --> observed: build results observed --> sealed: collect files } [*] --> check check --> solve: inputs OK solve --> finish finish --> [*]: result check --> failed: problem in inputs solve --> failed: program failed finish --> failed: bad output failed --> [*]: Diagnostic error ``` ## Layout Module dependencies (arrows are imports; every module also imports `kernel`): ```mermaid flowchart BT solver["solver
invoke()"] extraction --> solver & board buffers --> board simulation --> solver & board & extraction & buffers & observation ddr --> board & simulation pipeline --> solver & board & extraction & buffers & simulation & observation & ddr report --> pipeline & board & simulation & ddr adapters["adapters (/node)"] --> solver & board & buffers & pipeline & report ``` | module | owns | |---|---| | `kernel` | `Diagnostic`, safe ids, sha256, single-writer artifact ledger | | `solver` | `RunSolver` port; `invoke()` is the only way to run a solver | | `board` | Circuit JSON admission, stackup, ports, lanes, geometry (unmeshed) | | `extraction` | meshing, FastHenry/FasterCap decks, parsers, matrix checks, RLGC | | `buffers` | IBIS loading, SHA pinning, conversion | | `simulation` | declarations, node map, netlist, ngspice run, result records | | `observation` | waveform parsing, eye folding | | `ddr` | DDR assessment | | `pipeline` | `runPipeline` as typed stages, `modelingFromCircuitJson`, `PipelineResult` | | `report` | `generateReport` | | `adapters` | `/node` entry: native solver, IBIS file loading, output writing | Each module has one public `index.ts`. Imports are acyclic, and `node:*` appears only in `adapters`. ## Rename: `@tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline` → `@tscircuit/signal-integrity-pipeline` - The package name, repository URL, README, examples, docs and `scripts/test-package.mjs` use the new name. - ⚠️ **Not in this PR: `.github/workflows/pnpm-pver-release.yml`.** The pushing token lacks the `workflow` scope. `pnpm pack` now produces `tscircuit-signal-integrity-pipeline-.tgz`, but the workflow still uploads `tscircuit-pcb-spice-pipeline-$VERSION.tgz`, so **the next release would fail** until a maintainer applies this change: ```diff -# https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/releases/download/v/tscircuit-pcb-spice-pipeline-.tgz +# https://github.com/tscircuit/signal-integrity-pipeline/releases/download/v/tscircuit-signal-integrity-pipeline-.tgz - gh release create "$TAG" "tscircuit-pcb-spice-pipeline-$VERSION.tgz" \ + gh release create "$TAG" "tscircuit-signal-integrity-pipeline-$VERSION.tgz" \ ``` - **Unchanged:** the `pcb_spice` engine id (`spiceEngine="pcb_spice"`) and the `pcb_spice_channel` records. They are a Circuit JSON contract, so saved boards keep working. - **Follow-up needed:** - Rename the GitHub repo to `tscircuit/signal-integrity-pipeline` (deliberately left for later). GitHub redirects the old URLs. - `tscircuit/cli` pins the v0.1.8 tarball and imports `@tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline` in `cli/simulate/run-pcb-spice-simulation.ts`. It keeps working until it moves to the next release, which needs the new name. ## What changes for callers The same exports with the same signatures. Additions: - `Diagnostic`, `DiagnosticSubject` and `DiagnosticCode` are now exported as types. - Two new failures: `artifact_collision` (two writers to one path) and `report_missing_artifact` (the report references a missing file; it used to render `undefined`). - The `./node` export resolves to `dist/adapters`; the build still emits a `dist/node.js` shim. - `transmittedBits(value, code?)`: `code` is now typed to simulation's own codes. Runtime behaviour is unchanged. - 11 codes are dropped because only legacy code or tsx test helpers raised them: `clock_ui`, `eye`, `eyediagram`, `power`, `propagation`, `stimulus`, `tsx_board`, `tsx_reference`, `tsx_scope`, `tsx_simulation`, `tsx_supply`. `src/legacy/`, `tsx.ts` and `tsx-render.ts` move to `tests/support/`. ### Where the old files went | Old file(s) | New module | |---|---| | `schema.ts`, `circuit-schema.mjs`, `stackup.ts`, `subcircuit-scope.ts`, `geometry.ts`, `stage-returns.ts`, `copper.ts` (geometry half) | `board` | | `copper.ts` (mesh half), `extraction.ts`, `matrices.mjs`, `spice.ts` | `extraction` | | `model-source.ts`, IBIS part of `general-pipeline.ts` | `buffers` | | `declarations.ts`, `general-spice.ts`, `stimulus.ts`, ngspice part of `general-pipeline.ts` | `simulation` | | `metrics.mjs`, eye loop of `general-pipeline.ts` | `observation` | | `ddr.ts` | `ddr` | | `general-pipeline.ts`, `modeling.ts` | `pipeline` | | `report.ts`, `viewer.ts`, `viewer-client.ts` | `report` | | `node.ts` | `adapters` | | `solver.ts`, `hash.ts`, `Diagnostic` from `matrices.mjs` | `solver`, `kernel` | | `legacy/`, `tsx.ts`, `tsx-render.ts` | `tests/support/` (`eyediagram.mjs` dropped: only legacy code used it) | ## Guards | Rule | Enforced by | |---|---| | Stage order; no solver before validation | TypeScript compiler (`Chain<>`, `PureContext`) | | No code outside a module; index-only imports; acyclic; `node:*` only in adapters | `check-modules` S1–S6 | | Every module tested; every declared error code raised by a test | `check-modules` M1–M3 (no exemptions) | | Public exports; error-code set | `tests/compat` snapshots | | Every artifact path + sha256 identical to `main` | `tests/compat/golden` (passes on `main` and this branch) | | Eye fold keeps exactly the complete windows | `tests/observation/fold.test.ts` (brute-force reference) | | Temp dir always removed; timeout kills | `tests/adapters` (fault injection per step) | | Diagrams are Mermaid (workflow or state machine); README opening sections | `tests/tooling/docs.test.ts`, `AGENTS.md` | | Relative imports have no extension (`from './stages'`) | `tests/tooling/imports.test.ts`; the build adds `.js` back in `dist/` | | Code style (see **Lint** below) | `pnpm lint` | - **Compiler:** reordering `STAGES` fails with `not assignable to type 'never'`. Using `runSolver` before the validation line fails with `Property 'runSolver' does not exist`. - **`scripts/check-modules.ts`** (`pnpm check:modules`), derived from the filesystem and the TypeScript AST: - no code outside a module - imports only through each module's `index.ts` - no import cycles - `node:*` only in adapters - every module has tests, and every declared error code is raised by a test - `tools/exemptions.json` is empty - **`tests/compat/`:** - the export names - the error-code set - an artifact-path snapshot and a sha256 snapshot of every artifact, from two canned-solver scenarios The hash snapshot passes on both `main` and this branch. ## Lint (`pnpm lint`) Config in `eslint.config.mjs`. The three custom rules live in `tools/eslint/rules.mjs` and are tested in `tests/tooling/eslint-rules.test.ts`. | Rule | What it means | |---|---| | One variable per declaration, one statement per line | No `const a = 1, b = 2` and no `a(); b()` on one line | | JSDoc + typed signature | Every named function (`function f`, methods, `const f = () => …`) has a `/** … */` comment, a type on every parameter and a return type. Inline callbacks are exempt. | | No enums | Use a string-literal union or an `as const` object | | TypeScript files over 500 lines warn | Split the file, or opt out with `/* eslint-disable local/max-file-lines -- */` | | One test file per source file | `tests//.test.ts` tests `src//.ts`. `tests/compat`, `tests/tooling` and `tests/support` are exempt. | The existing code was brought in line: declarations and statements split onto their own lines, about 330 functions documented and typed, and 43 test files renamed or merged to match their source files (no test dropped). - **Warning left on purpose:** `src/extraction/mesh.ts` is 521 lines. It needs a decision: split it, or mark it as one to keep whole. - **Not in CI yet:** adding `pnpm lint` (and `pnpm check:vocabulary`) to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` needs a token with the `workflow` scope, the same as the release-workflow fix above. - **`results.html`:** the report embeds the chart viewer's code as text. That text now has the new JSDoc and line breaks, so its bytes differ from `main`, but the code does the same thing. Every hashed artifact is unchanged. ## Naming vocabulary (`pnpm check:vocabulary`) `tools/vocabulary.yaml` is the project's shared language. It has four sections: - **domain:** 103 words, each with a one-line meaning - **abbreviations:** 42 words, each with its expansion - **general:** 417 words - **avoid:** 15 words, each with the word to use instead (for example `ctx` → `context`) `scripts/check-vocabulary.ts` splits every name declared in `src/` into words (`foldProbeEye` → fold, probe, eye). It reports the share of names made only of dictionary words, overall and per module, and lists the unknown words with the most-used first. It fails below 85%. The target is deliberately not 100%: an unknown word is a question for a person (add it to the dictionary, or rename the code?). ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Names declared in src/] --> B[Split into words] B --> C{Every word in the dictionary?} C -- yes --> D[Name follows] C -- no --> E[Unknown words listed, most used first] D --> F{Share of names that follow is at least 85%?} E --> F F -- yes --> G[Pass] F -- no --> H[Fail] ``` Today the code scores **96.5%**. The lowest module is `extraction` at 90.6%, mostly from short variable names in `mesh.ts`. The dictionary was seeded from today's code, so its domain section should be reviewed as the project's intended language. ## Verification - `pnpm lint`: 0 errors, 1 warning (`mesh.ts` length) - `pnpm typecheck`: 0 errors - `pnpm check:vocabulary`: 96.5% (target 85%) - `pnpm test`: 295 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (the env-gated native test) - `pnpm check:modules`: exit 0 - `pnpm build`: ok - `pnpm test:package`: Node, cold-import (host actions denied), NodeNext declarations and Bun all pass - `test:native` was **not** run, because the native tools aren't installed locally. ## Open questions 1. **DDR status rule:** today a strobe-gate failure gives `not-evaluated` instead of letting the violation win. This PR keeps today's behaviour. Is that intended? 2. **#22 (FastHenry retries):** should `solver.invoke` allow a bounded number of retries and log each attempt, or should retries stay with the caller? 3. **Merge order:** this splits `copper.ts`, so #45, #47 and #4 will need a rebase onto `board/` and `extraction/`. Should those land first, or rebase after? 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: straightened-stages: derive wire-stage returns from pcb_stackup (stripline gets both planes)
description: This PR changes the handling of wire-stage returns in the signal integrity pipeline, allowing for derived returns from the PCB stackup when no profile is provided, specifically enabling correct modeling of striplines between ground planes.
body:
Fixes #50. `straightened-stages` needed a hand-written `straightened_stage_profiles` entry for every layer, and each entry allowed only one return bar. So a stripline between two ground planes (AM3352 DQS on `inner2`, with GND on `inner1` and `inner3`) couldn't be modelled correctly. ## Before / after This PR changes one box in the pipeline, highlighted below. Everything else, including the `routed-copper` fork, is unchanged. **Before** ```mermaid flowchart TD A["TSX → @tscircuit/core → circuit JSON"] --> B["validateCircuitRecords"] --> C["modelingFromCircuitJson
requires straightened_stage_profiles"] --> D["route lookup + stage list"] D --> F{"reduction?"} F -- routed-copper --> A1["routedCopperGeometry"] --> A2["groundMesh"] --> A3["copper decks"] F -- straightened-stages --> B1["stage cells"] --> B2["CHANGED: profile → 1 return box
hand-written, one plane only"]:::changed --> B3["fastHenryDeck / fasterCapDeck"] A3 --> S["solve twice + check"] B3 --> S S --> I["ibis-to-spice"] --> N["channel.cir → ngspice"] --> E(["eye diagram + results.html"]) classDef changed fill:transparent,stroke:#e5534b,stroke-width:4px ``` **After** ```mermaid flowchart TD A["TSX → @tscircuit/core → circuit JSON"] --> B["validateCircuitRecords"] --> C["modelingFromCircuitJson
NEW: profiles optional"]:::changed --> D["route lookup + stage list"] D --> F{"reduction?"} F -- routed-copper --> A1["routedCopperGeometry"] --> A2["groundMesh"] --> A3["copper decks"] F -- straightened-stages --> B1["stage cells"] --> B2{"NEW: profile for
this layer?"}:::changed B2 -- yes --> P["1 return box from profile
(as before)"]:::changed B2 -- "no · wire stage" --> G["NEW: return from pcb_stackup + GND pours
1 box per adjacent plane
stripline → 2 boxes, one conductor"]:::changed B2 -- "no · via stage" --> X["NEW: error, via needs a profile"]:::changed P --> B3["fastHenryDeck / fasterCapDeck
NEW: multi-part return"]:::changed G --> B3 A3 --> S["solve twice + check"] B3 --> S S --> I["ibis-to-spice"] --> N["channel.cir → ngspice"] --> E(["eye diagram + results.html"]) classDef changed fill:transparent,stroke:#2da44e,stroke-width:4px ``` ## Change When a wire stage's layer has no profile, its return comes from the board: - **Planes:** each directly adjacent copper layer that carries a pour on the reference ground net, reached from `channelReference` (`src/stage-returns.ts`). - **One 2 mm return bar per plane**, with height, thickness and εr from `pcb_stackup`. A stripline gets both planes. - **The bars form one `return` conductor:** - parallel `parts`, joined with `.equiv` at both ends in the FastHenry deck, with one `.external`; - one FasterCap conductor; - the DC analytic check sums the part areas. - **Lane spacing** is the median routed centre-to-centre distance when no profile declares it. - **Declared profiles still win.** Via stages still need an explicit `via` profile; the error now says so. - **No layer with ground next to it:** explicit `return_geometry` error asking for a profile. No props, core or circuit-json changes: `straightened_stage_profiles` is already optional there. Only the pipeline's own "profiles required" check is removed. ## Verification - **New `tests/stage-returns.test.mjs`:** - a derived microstrip return; - an explicit error when there's no adjacent ground plane; - stripline returns in both planes; - both decks treat the parts as one conductor. - **`pnpm typecheck`:** clean. - **`pnpm test`:** 173 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (pre-existing). - **Real board, AM3352 DQ0 on `top`** ([board PR](https://github.com/0hmX/am3352-ddr-track-a-local-dfm-wip-20261007/pull/9)): with the hand profile removed, the derived geometry is identical to the hand-written one (2 mm × 0.0152 mm bar, 0.1245 mm below, εr 4.1). That profile gave R 0.410 Ω, L 10.18 nH, C 3.32 pF and passes every extraction check. title: Scope channels across sibling subcircuits to their common subcircuit
description: Fixes simulation failure when channels cross sibling subcircuits by scoping them to their nearest common subcircuit.
body:
## Problem
A DDR write channel runs from the processor to the memory, and boards often keep those in sibling subcircuits under the board subcircuit. The AM3352 board does (`Processor` and `DDR3`). After the round-trip fix in #33, `tsci simulate` on that board fails with:

```
tsx_scope: BYTE0_WRITE_QUIET: selected pins cross saved subcircuits
```

Scopes were compared by exact innermost subcircuit:
- `serializeSimulation` rejected experiments, probes and nets whose pins sat in different subcircuits.
- Plan building in `declarations.ts` only accepted models, channel endpoints and probes in exactly the experiment's subcircuit.

So any cross-subcircuit channel was impossible.

## Change
- New `src/subcircuit-scope.ts` builds the saved subcircuit tree from `source_group` parentage. It provides `within(inner, outer)` and `common(scopes)` (nearest common subcircuit, with `undefined` as the unscoped root).
- `tsx-render.ts`:
  - Experiment scope = common subcircuit of its IBIS pin states.
  - Probe scope = common subcircuit of its signal and reference terminals.
  - Unscoped net scope = common subcircuit of its pins. An explicit `net.subcircuit_id` must still contain all its pins.
- `declarations.ts`: models, channel endpoints and probes are accepted when they are **contained in** the experiment scope.

Still strict: without an explicit experiment scope, models in several unrelated subcircuits are still rejected ("multiple modeled subcircuits require an explicit experiment scope"). Pins in unrelated top-level subcircuits only share the unscoped root.

## Tests
- `tests/subcircuit-scope.test.ts`: containment and nearest-common-ancestor cases, including an intermediate non-subcircuit group and unrelated roots.
- `tests/tsx.test.ts`: a driver and a receiver in sibling `CPU`/`RAM` subcircuits round-trip through `ImportedBoard`. The experiment is scoped to the board subcircuit, a RAM-local probe to `RAM`, and a CPU→RAM probe to the board. It fails before this change with `selected pins cross saved subcircuits`.
- `pnpm test`: 163 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.
- AM3352: with #33 and this change, `serializeSimulation` succeeds on the real board. The run then stops on core emitting schema-invalid records (`pcb_group.anchor_alignment: null`), which is being fixed in core separately.

title: Make ImportedBoard internal to this package
description: Removes public export of ImportedBoard and serializeSimulation, marking ImportedBoard as internal and documenting its unsupported status in tsci projects.
body:
## Why
`ImportedBoard` + `serializeSimulation` rebuild a saved board from Circuit JSON so simulation declarations can be attached to it. That's useful for this package's own tests. It isn't how tsci projects should simulate: they already author their boards in TSX and can put the declarations directly in their own `<board>`.

When a tsci project used it anyway (the AM3352 DDR board), two things went wrong:
- The CLI had to load this package from the user's project, so a fresh install failed with `Cannot find module '@tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/tsx'`.
- The rebuilt copy lost information. For example, duplicate switch pads became ambiguous selectors.

## Change
- Remove the public `./tsx` export. The helpers stay in `src/tsx.ts` for this package's tests.
- Mark `ImportedBoard` `@internal` and document that it isn't supported in tsci projects.
- README: replace the "TSX bridge" section with "Simulating a board", which says to declare models, transient experiments, stimuli, probes and eyes as children of `<board>`.
- The stackup diagnostic now says `on <board>` instead of `on <board>/<ImportedBoard>`.

This is a breaking change for anyone importing `@tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/tsx`. A companion tscircuit/cli PR rejects `ImportedBoard` entries with a clear message instead of loading this package from the project.

## Tests
- New `tests/package-exports.test.mjs`: the exports are exactly `.` and `./node`, and neither mentions `tsx`.
- `pnpm test`: 161 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean. `pnpm run test:package` passes (packed cold import, NodeNext declarations, Bun in-memory run).

title: Grade ring edges already split by the T-junction repair
description: Fixes TypeError during FasterCap deck construction by ensuring boundary grading handles existing ring edge pieces correctly after T-junction repair.
body:
## Problem
After #33–#39, the AM3352 run gets through routed-copper extraction and circuit-node construction. It then crashes while building the FasterCap deck:

```
TypeError: Spread syntax requires ...iterable not be null or undefined
    at splitEdge → meshPolygon → face → surfacePanels → copperFasterCapDeck → extractChannel
```

The failing polygon is a ground-pour island: a via-clearance arc whose apex (vertex 6) lies **exactly** on the island's outer edge 16→17 (x = −1.649946, t = 0.5).
1. `meshPolygon`'s T-junction repair correctly splits edge 16→17 at vertex 6.
2. Boundary grading then still calls `splitEdge(16, 17, …)` on the original edge, which no longer exists in `edgeTris`.

## Change
- Boundary grading walks the **existing pieces** of each ring edge: the edge itself, or the ordered chain of collinear vertices the repair inserted. Each graded point goes into the piece it falls in, and points that coincide with a piece endpoint are skipped.
- If a piece is genuinely missing, it fails with a `ground_geometry` diagnostic instead of a `TypeError`.
- Edges that were not split behave exactly as before.
- `meshPolygon` is exported so it can be tested directly, like `groundMesh` and `panelAspectLimit`.

## Tests
- New `tests/copper.test.ts` case uses the exact 19-vertex AM3352 ring captured from the failing run. It meshes at panel sizes 0.2, 0.02 and 0.005 mm, and the triangle area matches the ring's shoelace area to 1e-9. It fails before this change with the `TypeError`.
- `pnpm test`: 161 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.

title: Cut channel nets that are split into per-subcircuit records
description: Fixes channel net binding issues by grouping net records joined by net-only traces, allowing for proper cutting of redundant connections in subcircuits.
body:
## Problem
After #33/#35/#36/#37/#38, the AM3352 run gets through routed-copper extraction and then fails while building the circuit nodes:

```
channel_short: Extracted endpoints are shorted by another ideal source trace or reference
```

`circuitNodes` cuts the redundant one-port-to-net bindings of a two-terminal channel only when **both endpoints bind the same `source_net`**. Subcircuits scope net records, so on the AM3352 board the logical `DDR_D0` is three records:

```
CPU pin  --source_trace_255--> DDR_D0@Processor --source_trace_2743 (net-only)--> DDR_D0@board
RAM pin  --source_trace_591--> DDR_D0@DDR3      --source_trace_2831 (net-only)--> DDR_D0@board
```

The endpoints never bind the same net id, so nothing is cut. The union then joins CPU and RAM pins through the board-level net.

## Change
- Group net records joined by **net-only** traces (non-channel traces with no ports).
- Compare endpoint bindings by group, and apply the existing cut to every record in the group.
- The safety checks apply to the whole group:
  - `channel_short` if any record is ground;
  - `channel_net` if a trace links the group to an outside net or a port binds several nets;
  - `channel_fanout` if any other port binds into the group.
- A single shared net is a group of one, so the existing behavior is unchanged.

## Tests
- New `tests/general.test.mjs` case: the straight fixture with `DQ@cpu`/`DQ@ram`/`DQ@board` records arranged as above. The endpoints get distinct nodes and the board record is cut. Adding a third port tap on `DQ@board` still fails as `channel_fanout`. It fails before this change with `channel_short`.
- `pnpm test`: 161 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.

title: Pre-mesh routed copper into well-shaped FasterCap panels
description: Fixes ill-conditioned collocation system in FasterCap by pre-shaping routed copper panels, improving solver performance and accuracy.
body:
Fixes #28.

## Problem
The routed-copper FasterCap deck sent the solver huge, extremely thin panels:
- each 12.6 × 2.6 mm pour face as two sliver triangles, with a minimum angle of about 0.03°;
- 12.6 mm × 8 µm pour side walls;
- 10 mm × 35 µm trace walls.

The collocation system was badly conditioned. GMRES needed 470–1000+ iterations, C swung from 0.94 to 1.54 pF depending on `capacitanceTolerance`, and only 0.08 passed the reciprocity check. Even then C was 31% too low.

FasterCap flags alone can't fix this. Under `-a`, FasterCap ignores `-t`. Jacobi, two-level and Galerkin preconditioners, and fixed `-m` meshes all still stall or swing by ±30%.

## Fix
When `copperFasterCapDeck` gets extraction settings, as it does on the pipeline's routed-copper path, `surfacePanels` now pre-shapes the copper:
- **Faces** use a graded constrained-Delaunay mesh. Panel size is half the signal width at the signal and grows by 0.5 × distance, up to the existing `maxPanelLength`.
- **Side walls** are split so no panel is longer than 10 × the copper thickness.
- **An earcut T-junction** left by collinear via-hole edges is split at the vertex on it.

The closed copper solid and the area-preservation check are unchanged. No new user settings.

## Results (issue geometry, deck built by this branch's `copperFasterCapDeck`, pipeline flags `-a<tol> -ap -e`)
Reference C is 1.378 ± 0.003 pF. Two independent non-FasterCap dense-LU BEM solvers agree on it, and the 2D per-length value matches Hammerstad/Wheeler thick-strip formulas to within 0.2%.

| tolerance | before | after | GMRES iters (before → after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 | ✗ reciprocity 0.065 | ✓ 1.367 pF (−0.8%) | 473 → 11 |
| 0.08 | ✓ 0.953 pF (−31%) | ✓ 1.367 pF (−0.8%) | 723 → 11 |
| 0.05 | ✗ GMRES 1000-iter fail, 115 s | ✓ 1.361 pF (−1.2%) | 1000 → 12 |
| 0.03 | — | ✓ 1.335 pF (−3.2%) | → 16 |
| 0.02 | ✗ > 40 min | ✓ 1.340 pF (−2.8%) | → 18 |

Every FasterCap run finishes in under 0.4 s. The deck grows from 236 to about 9k input panels.

## Alternatives tried
- **Solver flags only:** no combination passes at every tolerance.
- **Modeling thin copper as zero-thickness sheets:** this fixes the conditioning, but C stays 5–12% off unless the panels are also well shaped. It could be an opt-in follow-up on top of this change.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 160 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped. Adds a test that checks graded faces, wall aspect ratio, `maxPanelLength` and an unchanged closed-solid volume.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- Not yet run: a full `tsci simulate` of the issue repro against this branch. The results above come from a reconstruction of the issue geometry run through `copperFasterCapDeck`.

title: Release to GitHub instead of npm
description: Changes the release process to create GitHub release assets instead of publishing to npm, addressing the issue of missing npm packages for the project.
body:
## Why
`@tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline` isn't on npm, and the workflow's token can't create it. Every "Publish to npm" run on `main` pushed a version tag and then failed:

```
npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@tscircuit%2fpcb-spice-pipeline
```

That left tags `v0.1.4`–`v0.1.6` with no package. Releases have been made by hand as GitHub release assets (`v0.1.3`, `v0.1.6`), and that's what tscircuit/cli depends on:
`https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/releases/download/v<version>/tscircuit-pcb-spice-pipeline-<version>.tgz`

## Change
`.github/workflows/pnpm-pver-release.yml`, renamed "Release":
- Same checks as before: typecheck, test, test:package.
- `pver release --git --package-json` bumps the version in the tag commit and pushes the tag. It doesn't publish to npm or push to `main`.
- The script checks out the newest `v*` tag, verifies `package.json` has the same version, runs `npm pack` (which builds), and runs `gh release create <tag> <tgz> --verify-tag --generate-notes`.
- If the tag already has a release (a rerun, or a `[norelease]` commit), it skips.
- Permissions are reduced to `contents: write`. `id-token` and `pull-requests` aren't needed any more, and neither is the npm token.

This takes a different approach from #27 (a `package-releases` branch served through jsDelivr), and both edit the same workflow file. Merging this one means closing #27.

## Validation
- `actionlint` 1.7.12 reports no issues for the release and CI workflows.
- I ran the release script in a scratch clone of `main`:
  - With real `gh`: `Release v0.1.6 already exists; nothing to publish.`
  - With `gh` stubbed so no release exists: it checks out `v0.1.6`, the version matches, it packs `tscircuit-pcb-spice-pipeline-0.1.6.tgz`, and it calls `gh release create v0.1.6 … --verify-tag --title v0.1.6 --generate-notes`.
  - The packed tarball's SHA-256 (`989c75f7…`) is identical to the manually published `v0.1.6` release asset.
