title: Accept board-level reference vias in pads of nested-subcircuit parts
description: Allows board-level vias in pads of nested subcircuit parts to be recognized as direct contacts for routed-copper extraction, resolving issues with ground connections.
body:
**Stacked on #35** (uses its `subcircuitTree`). Retarget to `main` after #35 merges.

## Problem
After #33/#35/#36/#37, routed-copper extraction on the AM3352 board stops at the CPU ground reference:

```
ground_connection: source_port_334: require one routed ground lead to a reference via/pour
```

`U1.A1` has a via-in-pad (`pcb_via_230`, top→inner1, barrel inside the inner1 `GND` pour). The via is board-level (`subcircuit_source_group_74`), but the pad belongs to `U1` inside the `Processor` subcircuit (`subcircuit_source_group_0`). Direct pad/via contacts required `via.subcircuit_id === port.subcircuit_id`, so the via was discarded. The code then looked for a routed lead, and A1 doesn't have one.

## Change
Accept a direct-contact via whose subcircuit **contains** the pad's subcircuit (`subcircuitTree(circuit).within(port, via)`). The physical checks are unchanged:
- barrel inside the pad;
- trace or net connected to the pin;
- span and plating;
- barrel inside ground copper.

A via owned by a nested subcircuit still can't serve a pad outside it.

## Tests
- New `tests/via-in-pad.test.ts` case: the via-in-pad fixture with both parts' pads moved into a child subcircuit, so the vias are board-level. Both reference contacts resolve to the via (contact radius 0.15 mm). The reverse case (vias nested, pads at board level) is still rejected with `ground_connection`. It fails before this change.
- `pnpm test`: 164 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.

title: Treat same-named per-subcircuit ground net records as one ground
description: Fixes ground net ambiguity by treating same-named per-subcircuit ground net records as a single ground, resolving extraction errors in routed copper geometry.
body:
## Problem
Subcircuits scope `source_net` records, so a board-wide `GND` appears once per subcircuit, with the records joined by traces. On the AM3352 board, the CPU ground ball `U1.A1` reaches **12** `GND` records (`Processor`, `DDR3`, …, and the board subcircuit). After the bridge and schema fixes (#33, #35, #36), routed-copper extraction stops with:

```
ground_net: The channel reference must connect to exactly one source_net marked is_ground
```

No board with subcircuits can meet that requirement. `routedCopperGeometry` already collects pours and vias across **every** connected net (`netIds`). The single `net` was only used for the report's `sourceNetId`/`sourceNetName` and an error message.

## Change
- Use one ground when the reference connects to several `is_ground` records that **all share one name**.
- Name it after the record the reference pin's own trace connects to.
- Differently named grounds shorted together (for example `AGND`/`DGND`) are still rejected as ambiguous.

The existing `ambiguous` case in `tests/copper.test.ts` keeps failing as before.

## Tests
- New `tests/copper.test.ts` case: the ground-plane fixture plus a same-named `GND` record in another subcircuit, tied through the receiver ground pin. Extraction succeeds, is named after the reference pin's own record, and uses the same pours. It fails before this change with `ground_net`.
- `pnpm test`: 161 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.

title: Accept saved core pcb_group and board-text records in schema validation
description: Fixes schema validation errors for saved core pcb_group and pcb_silkscreen_text records by handling null values and formatting numeric display offsets correctly.
body:
## Problem
After the bridge fixes (#33, #35), `tsci simulate` on the AM3352 board stops at schema validation, before any extraction:

```
circuit_schema: pcb_group pcb_group_0: anchor_alignment: Expected 'top_left' | … , received null
circuit_schema: pcb_silkscreen_text pcb_silkscreen_text_246: pcb_component_id: Required
```

On that board, core output fails circuit-json validation in these places:

| Record | Field | Count | Saved value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pcb_group` | `anchor_alignment` | 74 | `null` |
| `pcb_group` | `display_offset_x/y` | 7 | number |
| `pcb_silkscreen_text` | `pcb_component_id` | 20 | `null` (board-level text) |
| `pcb_component` | `display_offset_x/y` | 347 | number (already aliased here) |

The `pcb_silkscreen_text` override (`z.string().nullable()`) also *requires* the key. So the form current circuit-json specifies ("omitted for board- or group-level text") is rejected too.

## Change
Use the existing `compatible(...)` helper, which validates a normalized copy and returns the original record:
- `pcb_group`: drop `anchor_alignment: null` and format numeric display offsets as `"<n>mm"` before validation.
- `pcb_silkscreen_text`: drop `pcb_component_id: null` before validation, so both `null` and an omitted key validate.
- Numeric display-offset handling is shared with the existing `pcb_component` alias.

Saved records are never rewritten. Invalid values such as an unknown anchor or a numeric `pcb_component_id` are still rejected.

Core is also being fixed to stop emitting these forms. This PR keeps boards that were already saved working.

## Tests
- New `tests/circuit-schema.test.mjs` case covers both the legacy (`null`/numeric) and the circuit-json (`"center"`/string/omitted) forms of each field. It checks that records are left unchanged and that invalid values are still rejected. It fails before this change.
- `pnpm test`: 161 pass, 0 fail. `pnpm run typecheck` is clean.

title: RFC: <signalintegrity> and <signal> for signal integrity
description: Proposes a signal-level API for signal integrity that replaces the current hand-assembled pcb_spice API.
body:
Proposes a signal-level API for signal integrity that **replaces** the current hand-assembled `pcb_spice` API.

```tsx
<signalintegrity name="SI" bitRate="20Mbps">
  <signal name="DATA" driver=".TX > .Y" receiver=".RX > .A" />
</signalintegrity>
```

You name the signals; topology, coupled RLGC extraction, ground return, IBIS pin states, patterns, probes, eyes and DDR strobe sampling are derived from the board.

**Learning progression:** one `<signal>` (single-ended or `{ p, n }` differential) → two signals (coupled) → three signals (optionally one `quiet="low|high|off"` to measure NEXT/FEXT) → DDR with `strobe` and `mask`.

**Removed** (not deprecated): `ibisPinStates`, `pcbSpiceChannel` / `modeling.lanes`, `reduction`, `sections`, `extraction.*`, stage profiles, `passiveComponentRefs`/`termination`, per-pin `<analog.digitalstimulus>`/`<voltageprobe>`/`<analog.eyediagram>` for SI, `modeling.ddrAssessments`, hand-appended `pcb_stackup`, and the `simulation.config.ts` file. A full old→new table is in the RFC.

Contents:
- `rfcs/2026-11-08-signal-integrity-signal-api.md`: props, endpoint types, topology rules, `quiet`/`probe`/`mask`/`strobe` semantics, board requirements, results, Circuit JSON records, diagnostics, removed API, implementation plan, alternatives, open questions.
- `assets/2026-11-08-signal-integrity-signal-api/`: one example board per level (illustrative; they use the proposed elements and do not type-check yet).

This would supersede the SI-specific parts of #23 and #25.

Evidence: a user-land prototype that expands `<SignalIntegrity>`/`<Signal>` into today's primitives ran end to end with FastHenry, FasterCap and ngspice for one SE signal, a terminated differential pair, two and three coupled SE signals (including a quiet victim probed at both ends), and diff + SE. With the existing lane checks widened, four coupled conductors also ran.

The explosion menu includes a seconds-per-stage setting, PlayPauseReplay, previousnext stage buttons, and Reset. Scrubbing or stepping pauses playback, and closing the menu cancels animation. Playback evaluates a lightweight copy of the movement program and component poses, sharing immutable model geometry rather than cloning it each frame. The viewer also memoizes its serialized model identity. A local FLEX17 CPU benchmark measured pose evaluation at about 4 ms instead of 325 ms, and removes approximately 78 ms of repeated serialization per update. These timings are not an end-to-end FPS measurement. Adds the FLEX17 adjustable spur assembly as a self-contained Storybook sample with its 18 authored stages, based on https:flex17-tsx-adjustable-spur.seveibar.chatgpt.site. Validation: package build, full TypeScript check, five unit tests (including equivalence with core at 90 FLEX17 poses and geometry-sharing checks), and all five Playwright explosion tests pass. Local browser verification uses system Chromium and circuit-to-svg 0.0.454 to avoid the latest transitive packages incompatibility with the repositorys circuit-json override.
body:
Explosion stages can now play continuously, defaulting to two seconds per stage. The explosion menu includes a seconds-per-stage setting, Play/Pause/Replay, previous/next stage buttons, and Reset. Scrubbing or stepping pauses playback, and closing the menu cancels animation.

Playback evaluates a lightweight copy of the movement program and component poses, sharing immutable model geometry rather than cloning it each frame. The viewer also memoizes its serialized model identity. A local FLEX17 CPU benchmark measured pose evaluation at about 4 ms instead of 325 ms, and removes approximately 78 ms of repeated serialization per update. These timings are not an end-to-end FPS measurement.

Adds the FLEX17 adjustable spur assembly as a self-contained Storybook sample with its 18 authored stages, based on https://flex17-tsx-adjustable-spur.seveibar.chatgpt.site/.

Validation: package build, full TypeScript check, five unit tests (including equivalence with core at 90 FLEX17 poses and geometry-sharing checks), and all five Playwright explosion tests pass. Local browser verification uses system Chromium and circuit-to-svg 0.0.454 to avoid the latest transitive package's incompatibility with the repository's circuit-json override.

title: Reproduce invalid schematic positions from text-only groups in schFlex
description: Fixes invalid schematic positions caused by adding a child group containing only a schematic note inside schFlex, preventing surrounding components positions from becoming NaN.
body:
## Motivation
Found during schematic work for our pocket audio-player board. Adding a child group containing only a schematic note inside `schFlex` makes the surrounding components' positions and parent dimensions `NaN`. Users should be able to add explanatory notes without breaking automatic schematic placement.

In `Group_doInitialSchematicLayoutFlex`, the fallback bounds calculation finds no schematic components in the note group and returns non-finite dimensions.

description: Bumps the tscircuitcopper-pour-solver dependency to version 0.0.72 to fix copper spikes between rounded SMT pins and ensures proper rendering of multiple board pours by passing the owning PCB board ID to the solver.
body:
## Changes

- Bump `@tscircuit/copper-pour-solver` from `^0.0.67` to `^0.0.72` to pick up [the fix for copper spikes between rounded SMT pins](https://github.com/tscircuit/copper-pour-solver/pull/146).
- Pass the owning PCB board ID to the solver. Without it, `0.0.72` clips each panel pour against the first board, so the existing two-board regression fixture loses the second pour.

## Verification

- Confirmed the published `0.0.72` package includes the eFuse fix and that Core renders a straight clearance between the eFuse pins.
- Verified the panel fixture emits two pours, each with the expected 1 mm edge clearance.
- `bun run build` and `tsc --noEmit` passed.
- `bun test copper` produced 33 passes and one skip. Its 14 local snapshot mismatches reproduced on `main` with byte-identical diff images.

body:
Dense system diagrams braid neighboring wires when block faces and connection landing order follow coarse group geometry. Lay out subsystem contents independently, route around blocks and labels, and optimize adjacent landing slots—including swaps around block corners—against the complete diagram’s crossings, shared segments, spacing, bends, and length. Bound the search to 64 swaps and one final rerouting sweep.

Keep clear straight arrows and same-face return loops simple by placing their labels beside the wire. Horizontal connections retain inline labels when text fits. Regression assertions cover straight arrows and compact semicircular loops in all four page directions.

Round after optimization, letting curves use label padding while protecting the text. Preserve neighboring wire clearance without rejecting curves that move away from an already close wire. Check tangent continuity in the nested fixture, and use zero image-difference allowance for system snapshots so small routing changes cannot leave stale images. Emit optional connection colors and line styles. The RVBoy console and power fixtures check CPU landing order, wire intersections (including sampled cubic curves), and 3 mm separation between overlapping parallel runs. Dense graphs can still have crossings.

Use the released companion packages: `@tscircuit/props@^0.0.721`, `circuit-json@^0.0.548`, and `circuit-to-svg@^0.0.457`. Their PRs are merged: https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/992, https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/981, and https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/913. Remove the temporary Git dependency and build-script trust entry.

The props update requires complete courtyard polygons. Join legacy KiCad imports that store separate two-point courtyard edges into closed polygons before constructing components, preserving component/layer boundaries and leaving input records unchanged. Add a visual regression test for shuffled and reversed edges and reject disconnected chains.

Validation: 30 targeted tests pass across 28 files, covering all prior CI failure cases, system-block features, and courtyard import regression. TypeScript checking, dependency checking, and the ESM/declaration build pass locally. Browser checks find no overlaps among the 23 RVBoy connection labels, blocks, and headings. Existing schematic snapshots pass unchanged with the registry renderer and shared symbol definitions.

![RVBoy console](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/codex/system-diagram-wiring/tests/features/system-blocks/__snapshots__/system-blocks-rvboy-console.snap.svg)

![RVBoy power](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/codex/system-diagram-wiring/tests/features/system-blocks/__snapshots__/system-blocks-rvboy-power.snap.svg)

title: chore: adopt published courtyard importer and validation fixes
description: Updates dependencies for kicad-to-circuit-json and tscircuitprops, ensuring validation fixes and improved courtyard polygon handling.
body:
Ships merged fixes for https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/4772: https://github.com/tscircuit/kicad-to-circuit-json/pull/282 and https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/974.

Update `kicad-to-circuit-json` from `^0.0.142` to published `^0.0.149`, and `@tscircuit/props` from `^0.0.719` to published `^0.0.721` in both the development dependency and the existing matching override. No new override is added.

The importer joins a segmented footprint courtyard into a complete polygon. Props rejects fewer than three polygon points instead of allowing a later non-zero-area DRC failure. Core's dependency versions are copied into tscircuit; making this change in Core prevents a direct tscircuit edit from being overwritten by that synchronization.

Validation: seven existing courtyard/overlap/imported-rotation/local-KiCad-port tests pass (30 assertions); full typecheck passes. An installed-package probe confirms a two-point outline is rejected and TL3342 imports as one four-point courtyard. Refresh the existing Arduino before-inflation snapshot for the importer's separately merged rounded-pad radius correction: 122 pads gain their native KiCad corner radii; pad sizes, positions and all other SVG geometry are unchanged. Its 120 assertions pass with that snapshot. This repository does not track its generated Bun lockfile.

This dependency adoption covers local/imported files and validation. The separate remote `kicad:` footprint server still needs its already-merged #31 update deployed; the live endpoint currently returns four two-point contours. This PR does not redeploy, refresh or purge that service, and does not add Core courtyard stitching. No merges or releases performed.

title: Use outgoing segment width when checking trace-to-hole clearance
description: Fixes a bug where a wider terminal vertex could cause the hole-clearance checker to misinterpret a positive gap as an overlap, suppressing a real clearance violation.
body:
A wider terminal vertex can make the hole-clearance checker mistake a positive gap for an overlap and suppress a real clearance violation. Use the outgoing wire’s width (including its own taper bounds), matching the overlap checker after #535.

The regression reproduces a 0.100 mm trace-to-hole gap against a 0.200 mm rule, and includes safe-gap and true-overlap controls.

Validation: 758 tests pass (8,471 assertions), TypeScript, package build, and formatting pass.

title: Use outgoing wire width when checking trace clearance
description: Fixes false clearance errors on valid variable-width power traces by using the outgoing wires width during overlap checks.
body:
A narrow segment followed by a wider segment inherited the wider segment’s width during overlap checks. This produces false clearance errors on valid variable-width power traces, including the RP2040 simplification regression in tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3580.

Use the outgoing wire’s width and its own taper bounds. Added widened/tapered negative controls and the exact captured RP2040 Circuit JSON, with before/after snapshots cropped to the reported gap.

Validation: 757 tests pass; build and formatting pass. Independent geometry measurement of the affected trace pair finds a 0.153 mm minimum gap, while the old checker reported 0.040 mm.

title: Add direct engineering drawing SVG and PNG downloads
description: Add Engineering Drawing PNG and SVG downloads to the Download  Images menu on package pages and in the editor, allowing users to download single images or ZIPs of multiple drawings.
body:
Add **Engineering Drawing PNG** and **Engineering Drawing SVG** to the existing **Download → Images** menu on package pages and in the editor. Selecting either action downloads a single image when the circuit has one drawing, or automatically downloads a ZIP containing every drawing when there are multiple pages. There is no drawing picker or extra dialog.

![Running tscircuit.com application showing engineering drawing PNG and SVG downloads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rushabhcodes/tscircuit.com/5992e80e9101869f45fe8db970d82111a9357751/pr-5753/engineering-drawing-download-menu.png)

*Actual local application with an engineering-drawing fixture; both download actions are enabled.*

PNG exports reuse the existing browser-canvas SVG-to-PNG converter, extracted into a shared helper also used by schematic, PCB, assembly, and pinout PNG downloads. Archive filenames include the format, and colliding sanitized page filenames receive numbered suffixes so every sheet is preserved. Empty circuits disable both drawing actions, and progress/errors use the existing download toasts. Single-file export returns directly; JSZip is created only for multiple sheets. The shared PNG converter releases SVG URLs after conversion and rejects encoding errors so downloads can recover instead of hanging.

Use the published **@tscircuit/drawing-viewer 0.0.5** CDN package, which includes the renderer API from merged [drawing-viewer PR #9](https://github.com/tscircuit/drawing-viewer/pull/9). The temporary Git commit dependency has been removed.

Existing patterns:

- [Existing PNG downloads render SVG and rasterize it through a canvas](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/blob/b30054a42079797f0e65b987e65b871a41686f16/src/lib/download-fns/download-circuit-png.ts#L32-L80). Drawing PNG downloads now share that converter.
- [Fabrication downloads package multiple generated files with JSZip](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/blob/b30054a42079797f0e65b987e65b871a41686f16/src/lib/download-fns/download-fabrication-files.ts#L17-L59).
- [Altium downloads load their converter on demand and save the generated artifact](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/blob/b30054a42079797f0e65b987e65b871a41686f16/src/lib/download-fns/download-altium-files.ts#L5-L24).
- [`3d-viewer` publicly exports its SVG converter alongside its React viewer](https://github.com/tscircuit/3d-viewer/blob/main/src/index.tsx#L1-L2), the precedent for the shared renderer API.

Validation:

- Manually verified the [Vercel preview deployment](https://tscircuit-l3p4avra3-tscircuit.vercel.app/) using actual rendered circuits: a single sheet downloads directly as SVG or PNG; two sheets download as an SVG ZIP or PNG ZIP.
- Opened both archives and confirmed each contains both sheets with the expected filenames and titles. Decoded the downloaded PNGs: valid 1123 × 794 images, visually checked for board geometry and title block.
- Reproduce with the [one-sheet example](https://tscircuit-l3p4avra3-tscircuit.vercel.app/editor?snippet_type=board#data:application/gzip;base64,) or [two-sheet example](https://tscircuit-l3p4avra3-tscircuit.vercel.app/editor?snippet_type=board#data:application/gzip;base64,): click **Run**, then **Download → Images → Engineering Drawing SVG/PNG**. No registry write or login is required.
- Typecheck and `git diff --check` pass. Vercel deployed the application successfully.

title: Add explosion MP4 export with a committed real-assembly video test
description: Adds tsci export assembly.circuit.tsx --format explosion-mp4 -o assembly.mp4 (also accepts Circuit JSON). Playback uses the serialized explosion program through circuit-json-to-gltf and PoppyGL, including grouped stage targets, sequential movement and the exporters embedded guide lines. A fixed orthographic camera fits every move endpoint, including outward-and-return movements. Stage captions and configurable movementhold durations make each step readable.
body:
Adds `tsci export assembly.circuit.tsx --format explosion-mp4 -o assembly.mp4` (also accepts Circuit JSON). Playback uses the serialized explosion program through circuit-json-to-gltf and PoppyGL, including grouped stage targets, sequential movement and the exporter’s embedded guide lines. A fixed orthographic camera fits every move endpoint, including outward-and-return movements. Stage captions and configurable movement/hold durations make each step readable.

Requires FFmpeg with libx264 on PATH; output is browser-compatible H.264/YUV420p with fast-start metadata. Options: `--fps`, `--width`, `--height`, `--stage-duration`, `--hold-duration`. FFmpeg is installed for CI tests. PoppyGL’s development version mirrors tscircuit’s existing 0.0.38 pin so Bun cannot hoist the older helper version that ignores explosion extras; no new production npm dependency.

The test commits a [6.5-second RP2040/NEMA17 video](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/blob/feat/export-explosion-video/tests/cli/export/__snapshots__/rp2040-explosion.mp4), using the original routed PCB, real motor/bolts, cover and spacers with pinned offline model bytes. The NEMA17 and M3 bolt models come from [MIT-licensed jscad-electronics](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/blob/main/LICENSE). It lifts cover and bolts together, then separates bolts, motor and spacers. Tests decode the output, assert codec, size, frame count/rate and duration, and compare both the generated and committed video's storyboards, including an intermediate pose. Color conversion and H.264 encoding use reproducible CPU-independent settings; the PNG comparisons retain the repository's normal tolerance. title: Remove copper spikes between adjacent rounded SMT pins
description: Fixes copper spikes that occur between adjacent rounded SMT pins by bridging the clearances between overlapping pads, ensuring a smooth copper pour without sharp edges.
body: Stacked on #145. The NEMA23 eFuse has 0.5 mm pin pitch and 0.25 mm top pour clearance. The expanded pad capsules are about 0.78 mm across the row, so they overlap. Subtracting their union leaves a sharp copper tooth about 0.093 mm beyond the exposed ground pad edge. For consecutive, equally sized pill pads in the same footprint and row, fill the recess between overlapping clearance capsules. The solver adds a rectangle between their common tangents, making the combined clearance their convex hull. The original clearances remain part of the area subtracted from the pour. A same-net pin interrupts the row, and separated clearances or pads on different footprints are processed individually. Regression coverage includes the eFuse geometry, a rotated row, separated clearances, aligned pads on separate footprints, and a same-net pin between two different-net pins. Two existing RP2040 motor controller snapshots show the same clearance change. ## Verification - The corrected eFuse assertion fails on #145 and passes with this change. - Re-solving the published NEMA23 v1.4.20 Circuit JSON moved all five marked midpoint boundaries from x ≈ 11.557 mm to x = 11.650003 mm, aligned with the exposed pad edge. The pour still covers the exposed pad. - `bun test` (113 passing), `tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, and `bun run format:check`.

title: fix: select owning PCB board for panel copper pours
description: Fixes a limitation in the Circuit JSON converter that caused explicit pours on secondary PCB boards to be clipped against their sibling boards, by allowing selection of the owning PCB board for each pour.
body:
The Circuit JSON converter always selected the first `pcb_board`, so an explicit pour on the second board of a panel could be clipped against its sibling and disappear. This is the underlying converter limitation exposed while adopting board-outline clipping in tscircuit/core#5277, related to tscircuit/core#4703.

Add optional `pcb_board_id` to `ConvertCircuitJsonToInputProblemOptions`. Each options entry resolves its own board before computing bounds and physical-board clipping. Omission preserves first-board selection for existing callers; a supplied ID that is not found throws instead of silently using another board. The full Circuit JSON remains available for connectivity and obstacles. The existing batch subcircuit requirement is unchanged.

The regression contains a translated rectangular board and a separate chamfered board, with oversized explicit pours. The first commit records the actual broken snapshot; the fix updates that same snapshot to show copper on both boards. It checks emitted bounds, 0.5 mm edge/chamfer clearance, reversed Circuit JSON order, default selection, and missing IDs. Both new tests fail against main's converter; all 108 tests pass with the fix (4,146 assertions). Full typecheck, ESM/declaration build, changed-file formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

Once merged and published, Core can pass its owning `pcb_board_id` and remove the board-record filtering workaround in #5277. No Core changes, dependency bumps, releases or merges are included here.

title: Expose drawing SVG renderer for downloads
description: Expose the existing SVG renderer for downloads, allowing users to export drawings as SVG files either for all sheets or a specific sheet using a new API.
body:
tscircuit.com’s download menu needs SVG output, while this package currently exports only the React viewer. The existing private renderer already handles selected-part geometry, sections, dimensions, and glTF scene resolution. Expose that renderer through a lazy-loaded public `renderDrawingPages` API so the website can reuse it for single-sheet and all-sheet downloads. Calling the lower-level drawing converter directly would still require duplicating this package’s scene resolver and part-ownership filtering in the website.

Add an optional `drawingPageId` to export one sheet; omitting it renders every sheet in document order. Export the option/output types and document the API. The implementation remains in its existing module and loads only when rendering is requested.

Existing patterns:

- **Viewer package exposing an SVG renderer:** [`3d-viewer/src/index.tsx`](https://github.com/tscircuit/3d-viewer/blob/main/src/index.tsx#L1-L2) publicly exports [`convertCircuitJsonTo3dSvg`](https://github.com/tscircuit/3d-viewer/blob/main/src/convert-circuit-json-to-3d-svg.ts). This is the precedent for exposing rendering alongside the React viewer.
- **Loading an exporter when a download is requested:** [tscircuit.com’s existing Altium download helper](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/blob/b30054a42079797f0e65b987e65b871a41686f16/src/lib/download-fns/download-altium-files.ts#L5-L13) dynamically imports the public converter API. This is the precedent for keeping conversion code out of the initial download-menu load.

Validation: public-entrypoint renderer tests pass, including selected-sheet export when another sheet’s geometry is unavailable; existing section, dimension, and board-isolation tests pass. Typecheck and formatting pass.

Used by [tscircuit.com PR #5753](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/pull/5753).

The KiCad footprint server cannot deploy the already-merged courtyard importer update (#31): Vercel rejects the project's discontinued Node.js 20 selection before dependency installation or compilation.

Set `engines.node` to `26.x`. Vercel documents that this field overrides the project's Node.js setting: https://vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes/node-js/node-js-versions#version-overrides-in-packagejson

Failure evidence: deployment `dpl_3gQgeabSERC5YooF3XXH4K9sKWSb`, main commit `242e752`, reports: “Node.js Version \"20.x\" is discontinued and must be upgraded. Please set Node.js Version to 26.x in your Project Settings to use Node.js 26.”

The GitHub test check and Vercel preview deployment both pass on this commit; the preview confirms the Node.js 26 build succeeds. Local tests ran under Bun 1.4.3. No project settings, live caches, or deployments were changed manually.

After merge, the normal successful production deployment is still required before the fixed importer reaches browser KiCad footprint requests. This removes the first confirmed deployment blocker; any subsequent build error must be assessed from its own logs.

title: Load Manifold and circuit-generation code only when needed
description: Load Manifold and circuit-generation code only when needed to optimize performance by importing geometry code on demand based on user input.
body:
GLB scenes were still importing geometry code through the renderer and assembly/TSX helpers. CadViewer now imports the Manifold renderer on demand, and the assembly and child-conversion hooks load core only for TSX children or authored explosion programs. GLB URL and ArrayBuffer inputs bypass both paths, including when Circuit JSON metadata is also supplied; ordinary JSCAD JSON scenes do not load Manifold either.

The Circuit JSON dependency and override are aligned with the current SVG dependency so a fresh install resolves the system-schema exports used during browser builds.

Validation:
- Production bundle and declaration generation succeed; the bundle loads in Node.
- Type checking and formatting of changed files pass.
- Browser tests block Manifold requests for GLB URL/byte scenes and JSCAD, then verify that Manifold is requested when switching to its JSON renderer and that a failed runtime does not block switching back to GLB.
- GLB URL/byte checks also pass against the built bundle.
- Targeted unit coverage exercises GLB loading/disposal, assembly playback, lazy TSX conversion, and input replacement.

Related website change: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/pull/5756 removes the Circuit JSON wait for an explicitly selected GLB. Consumers must pick up the released viewer version to receive the library’s lazy-loading change.

title: Add GBA explosion example with cover rotation and control assemblies
description: Adds an overhead Game Boy Advance dual RP2350 explosion example with a 180 front-cover flip and separate analog-stick, speaker, and button removal stages. The thirteen-stage sequence removes user accessories first, parks each assembly on the left, flips the cleared front assembly inside-up, then removes its internal modules. Reverse playback reassembles the modules and flips the cover closed. The viewer now accepts optional assemblyExplosionRotations cues: axis, signed angle, and a world-space pivot attached to an authored move. Absolute transforms support scrubbing, reverse playback, late-loaded models, and Reset without rebuilding geometry or accumulating orientation drift. Guide lines follow the rotation arc. The rotation API is documented; it is a viewer extension supplied alongside cores translation-only circuit JSON. The example is pinned to absegameboy-advance-dual-rp23500.3.0-review.8. It preserves the routed PCB and model transforms, includes native TSX, serialized rotation cues, reproducible exporters and clearance checks, and loads assets from the public registry. This PR does not republish the registry package. Remaining extraction limitations: the initial battery-doorrear-shell and front-shellpower-switch collisions remain. Continuous bounds checks clear all parking paths and the full cover flip. A rendered-mesh audit at 0.25 mm travel intervals found no additional collisions in the added motions. The speaker comes out before the Select button to clear its retainer; the volume wheel stays with the cover because its extraction catches on the cover. Existing model contacts and findings are recorded in the fixture; this is not a fully collision-free assembly procedure. Validation: 15 unit tests covering pivot rotation, subsequent world-space motion, geometry sharing, arc anchoring, late loads, reset, source regeneration, complete group motions, PCB invariance, and swept clearance; three Chromium tests covering existing playback, guidelines, reverse, the halffull cover flip, subsequent module removal, backward scrubbing, and reset; TypeScript and library build.
body:
Adds an overhead Game Boy Advance dual RP2350 explosion example with a 180° front-cover flip and separate analog-stick, speaker, and button removal stages. The thirteen-stage sequence removes user accessories first, parks each assembly on the left, flips the cleared front assembly inside-up, then removes its internal modules. Reverse playback reassembles the modules and flips the cover closed.

The viewer now accepts optional `assemblyExplosionRotations` cues: axis, signed angle, and a world-space pivot attached to an authored move. Absolute transforms support scrubbing, reverse playback, late-loaded models, and Reset without rebuilding geometry or accumulating orientation drift. Guide lines follow the rotation arc. The rotation API is documented; it is a viewer extension supplied alongside core's translation-only circuit JSON.

The example is pinned to `abse/gameboy-advance-dual-rp2350@0.3.0-review.8`. It preserves the routed PCB and model transforms, includes native TSX, serialized rotation cues, reproducible exporters and clearance checks, and loads assets from the public registry. This PR does not republish the registry package.

**Remaining extraction limitations:** the initial battery-door/rear-shell and front-shell/power-switch collisions remain. Continuous bounds checks clear all parking paths and the full cover flip. A rendered-mesh audit at ≤0.25 mm travel intervals found no additional collisions in the added motions. The speaker comes out before the Select button to clear its retainer; the volume wheel stays with the cover because its extraction catches on the cover. Existing model contacts and findings are recorded in the fixture; this is not a fully collision-free assembly procedure.

Validation: 15 unit tests covering pivot rotation, subsequent world-space motion, geometry sharing, arc anchoring, late loads, reset, source regeneration, complete group motions, PCB invariance, and swept clearance; three Chromium tests covering existing playback, guidelines, reverse, the half/full cover flip, subsequent module removal, backward scrubbing, and reset; TypeScript and library build.

title: Add reverse playback and guideline visibility controls
description: Adds a Play In Reverse button to the explosion menu and a Show guidelines checkbox to control the visibility of explosion lines during playback.
body:
Adds a **Play In Reverse** button to the explosion menu. It plays from the current position back to assembled using the configured seconds per stage. At assembled, it starts from fully exploded. Users can switch from forward to reverse playback without resetting the position; Pause, scrubbing, and Reset still stop playback.

A **Show guidelines** checkbox, enabled by default, lets users hide or restore the explosion lines without changing the current position or interrupting playback. Hidden guidelines skip line-position updates.

Validation: forward and reverse Playwright playback tests, the FLEX17 guideline visibility browser check, package build, and TypeScript check. Browser tests use system Chromium and the existing local circuit-to-svg 0.0.454 workaround.

title: Fix initial camera framing for assemblies without a PCB
description: Fixes initial camera framing for CAD assemblies without a PCB, ensuring proper geometry bounds are respected during rendering.
body:
Opening a boardless CAD assembly such as FLEX17 with empty session storage starts the camera inside the model at `[5, -5, 5]`. Frame the rendered component and cable bounds as geometry loads in both Manifold and JSCAD.

Initial fitting respects restored sessions, user input, and explicitly authored camera commands. This preserves fixtures such as the gimbal phone holder, where an embedding app chooses the view through `onCameraControllerReady`. Click-to-interact controls inherit the fitted target, and orthographic zoom is persisted for reloads.

The diff contains six production source files.

Validation performed locally with temporary harnesses:
- Compared 53 existing Storybook fixtures across 124 renderer/projection cases against main (`c5fcaf8`), checking camera state, mesh bounds/materials, and screenshots. Results: 112 unchanged comparisons, 8 intended framing improvements for FLEX17/staged assemblies, and 4 existing fixture errors reproduced on both versions. No unexpected differences remain.
- Coverage includes off-origin boards and board-size switching, panels, faux boards, holes/cutouts, rotated components, flex/folded PCBs, sheet-metal assemblies, cables, local GLBs, and authored camera positions for the phone holder and RP2040 assembly. Existing JSCAD panel/orthographic clipping matches main.
- The 4 existing errors affect the legacy Simple and ClickToInteract stories in both engine settings (`getViaHolesAtExposedPads` encounters missing layer data).
- 33 targeted unit tests and 9 Chromium interaction checks pass, covering camera/session restoration, centered presets, GLB replacement, infinite dolly, explosion scrubbing, and click-to-interact.
- Type checking, formatting, package build, Node bundle loading, and all active PR CI checks pass.

Browser verification used local source because the reported Vercel preview domain is blocked in the cloud environment.

title: Keep explosion guides connected to moving components
description: Fixes explosion guide lines detaching from components when geometry is offset from CAD origin by anchoring movement paths to rendered component bounds and updating guides accordingly.
body:
Explosion guide lines could appear detached when a component's geometry was offset from its declared CAD origin, as in FLEX17. Anchor the authored movement paths to the rendered component bounds so their endpoints follow the moving parts, including through nested model and scene transforms.

Update guides after applying component offsets, wait for asynchronously loaded geometry, and omit guides for absent components. Reuse line geometry buffers and cached mesh bounds during playback instead of recreating GPU resources each frame.

Validation: five unit tests and all five explosion browser tests pass, including FLEX17 endpoint checks at partial and complete stages. Package build and full TypeScript check pass. Browser checks use system Chromium and the local circuit-to-svg 0.0.454 workaround documented in the preceding playback PR.

title: Fix missing components when schFlex contains text-only groups
description: Fixes issue where text-only groups inside schFlex cause neighboring components to have invalid positions, resulting in their disappearance from the schematic.
body:

A text-only group inside `schFlex` gives neighboring components invalid (`NaN`) positions, making them disappear from the schematic. This fixes the issue found during our audio-board investigation and reproduced in #5287.

Before, bounds calculation assumed every group contained components. After, text-only groups use their note bounds or explicit dimensions, empty groups have finite bounds, and notes move with their groups.

Updates the merged reproduction into a passing regression test, with coverage for empty groups and nested, anchored, rotated notes in column layout.

title: Constrain reconciler peer to the tested React-compatible version
description: Constrain the react-reconciler peer dependency to 0.31.0 to resolve ERESOLVE errors during npm install with React 19.1.0.
body:
`jscad-fiber` requires React/React DOM 19.1.0 but declares `react-reconciler: "*"`. A fresh npm install selects reconciler 0.34.0, whose React peer requires `^19.3.0`, and fails with ERESOLVE. This blocks npm consumers such as the Vercel deployment for https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-electronics/pull/513.

Constrain the reconciler peer to `^0.31.0` and refresh the root peer declaration in `bun.lock`. This is the reconciler version already selected by the repository's existing lockfile and test setup; its React peer is `^19.0.0`, which supports the declared React 19.1.0. Later reconciler minor versions use React internals that this package has not qualified.

Validation:
- Reproduced the ERESOLVE failure in a fresh npm consumer using the published fiber 0.0.93 package and React/React DOM 19.1.0.
- Packed this branch and verified `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts --strict-peer-deps` succeeds for that consumer and for the complete jscad-electronics manifest. The resolved reconciler is 0.31.0.
- All 32 existing tests passed; `bun run build:lib`, TypeScript, and whitespace checks passed.

Only the peer constraint and lockfile metadata change. After release, consumers need to select the new fiber version explicitly: their `^0.0.93` range will not admit the next `0.0.x` release.

Read public received expenses across all creation dates. Match recipient account ID plus exact contribution-period references so September work paid in November still belongs to September. This remains a report, not complete duplicate-payment protection or ownership verification.

title: Render PCB placement errors with support-region highlights
description: PCB support errors from tscircuitchecks are pcb_placement_error records. The PCB renderer previously skipped that type even when shouldDrawErrors was enabled, so the faulty regions were invisible. Render located placement errors above the PCB layers. Diagnostics with region widthheight receive a translucent red fill and dashed border; support errors show a short label and surviving-tab count. A native SVG title and accessible label retain the full diagnostic. Location-only errors receive a marker, and missingnonfinite locations are not drawn. Existing shouldDrawErrors visibility controls apply. The regression fixture contains the original basic-usbc-devices panel geometry and four actual support-check results. Visual snapshots cover highlighted regions, hidden errors, and location-onlymissing-location errors. The matching checks change adds region bounds: https:github.comtscircuitcheckspull539. Existing diagnostics with only a center still render without that update. Usage: ts const errors  checkPcbBoardSupport(circuitJson) const svg  convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg(...circuitJson, ...errors,  shouldDrawErrors: true, )  Validation: 13 PCB error-rendering tests across nine files pass, including the three new visual snapshots. Snapshots were rendered and visually inspected, then tests rerun without updating. TypeScript and package build pass. The checks-side bounds change passes its 15 focused regressions.
body:
PCB support errors from tscircuit/checks are `pcb_placement_error` records. The PCB renderer previously skipped that type even when `shouldDrawErrors` was enabled, so the faulty regions were invisible.

Render located placement errors above the PCB layers. Diagnostics with region width/height receive a translucent red fill and dashed border; support errors show a short label and surviving-tab count. A native SVG title and accessible label retain the full diagnostic. Location-only errors receive a marker, and missing/nonfinite locations are not drawn. Existing `shouldDrawErrors` visibility controls apply.

The regression fixture contains the original basic-usbc-devices panel geometry and four actual support-check results. Visual snapshots cover highlighted regions, hidden errors, and location-only/missing-location errors. The matching checks change adds region bounds: https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/539. Existing diagnostics with only a center still render without that update.

Usage:
```ts
const errors = checkPcbBoardSupport(circuitJson)
const svg = convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg([...circuitJson, ...errors], {
  shouldDrawErrors: true,
})
```

Validation: 13 PCB error-rendering tests across nine files pass, including the three new visual snapshots. Snapshots were rendered and visually inspected, then tests rerun without updating. TypeScript and package build pass. The checks-side bounds change passes its 15 focused regressions.

title: fix: unblock package update with verified KiCad pad-radius snapshot
description: Fixes the package update failure due to KiCads native rounded-pad radii preservation, ensuring accurate PCB-import snapshots and geometry validation.
body:
The package update in #5649 fails the Joule Thief PCB-import snapshot because kicad-to-circuit-json now preserves KiCad's native rounded-pad radii. Carry that update forward with the reviewed renderer-generated snapshot and explicit geometry regressions.

The upstream correction (tscircuit/kicad-to-circuit-json#281, released in 0.0.146) removes an erroneous division by two. In the final eval SVG, the only meaningful differences are rx/ry on nine plated pads. One silkscreen path also differs by at most 2.85e-14 SVG units. All 1,544 SVG elements remain present.

Investigation compared importer 0.0.142 against 0.0.149 on the repository's public Joule Thief fixture: board outline, component placement, all 136 imported traces, 32 imported vias, ports, nets and copper pours are unchanged. The importer also contains the intentional joined-courtyard fix (#282), reducing 212 segment records to 45 contours without changing PCB copper.

The integration test now asserts board dimensions, 53 components, 220 SMT pads, 136 traces, and all six SW1 plated-pad corner radii against the authored 3 × 1.6 mm / 0.1785714286 KiCad values. Parts lookup is stubbed because this geometry test does not need supplier data. No matcher tolerances or production code change.

Validation:
- Reproduced the original snapshot mismatch locally.
- Inspected the actual raster diff and before/after SVGs; checked changed attributes numerically.
- Updated integration test passes: 16 assertions.
- Complete `bun run build` passes (Bun 1.4.4).
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, repository formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Full remote matrix passes on f6a6582: all seven Bun Test groups, Type Check, Format Check, Playwright, Webworker Imports and Packaged Fabricator Engine are green. The original examples job was canceled after the features failure. The first full run here exposed the same stale pad radii in example26's multiple-subcircuit snapshot; that second snapshot is now reviewed and refreshed too (nine pad-radius changes, unchanged 1,569 elements, path rounding below 5.69e-14 SVG units). Both targeted tests pass together: 17 assertions. Both tests stub unrelated supplier lookups.

This is a replacement candidate for #5649; neither PR was merged or closed. No snapshots were accepted without checking their source geometry.

body:
The static build viewer placed its file selector and gallery button inside `leftHeaderContent`, leaving navigation beside File/View instead of centered. This is visible on [Compact USB Homing Modules](https://usb-homing-modules-compact.seveibar.chatgpt.site/#file=boards%2Fpanel.circuit.json), which uses RunFrame 0.0.3169.

Add an optional `centerHeaderContent` slot with three equal desktop columns so unequal side controls cannot shift navigation. On narrow screens navigation gets its own centered row. Apply the same layout to failed-file recovery and regenerate the bundled CSS. Existing previews without center content retain their flex layout.

Validation:
- All 92 Bun tests pass; TypeScript check passes (8 GB Node heap).
- CSS and standalone production builds pass; changed TSX formatting and diff checks pass.
- Chromium checks against the site's HTML/data with the locally built bundle: centered navigation and no horizontal overflow at 320, 390, 768, 1024, and 1440px; file switching and gallery navigation work.
- Long filenames, failed file loading, and single-file mode also checked. PCB rendering itself could not be verified because headless Chromium has no WebGPU adapter.

The hosted site remains pinned to 0.0.3169 and will need its dependency updated after release.

Preview: [Open the static build viewer directly](https://runframe-git-fix-center-static-viewer-file-navigation-tscircuit.vercel.app/renderer.html?fixtureId=%7B%22path%22%3A%22examples%2Fexample31-static-build-viewer.fixture.tsx%22%2C%22name%22%3A%22LoadingWithoutCustomFetch%22%7D&locked=true#file=index.tsx). title: Preserve polygon precision through copper pour clipping
description: Removes manual rounding in polygon normalization to preserve precision in copper pour clipping, ensuring compliance with a requested board-edge margin of 0.2 mm.
body:
A requested 0.2 mm board-edge margin can become 0.199998922476 mm because polygon normalization and Manifold conversion round the input outline, clearance obstacles, and output vertices to a 1e-6 mm grid.

Remove that manual rounding in the existing `polygon-ring.ts` conversion path. Manifold accepts floating-point polygon coordinates and handles clipping precision internally. Keep the existing scaling, finite-coordinate validation, duplicate/closing-point cleanup, winding normalization, and degenerate-ring rejection. The reproduced gap becomes 0.199999999999993 mm, within the existing check's numerical tolerance.

The TSX repro changes from asserting the recorded undershoot to requiring a clean clearance check and a measured gap of at least `0.2 - 1e-9`. Both snapshots display the actual measured gap to 12 decimal places: `0.199998922476 mm` before and `0.200000000000 mm` after. No margins or checker tolerances are changed.

Stacked on #149: review and merge the repro first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

Fixes https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/5301.

Validation:
- `bun test` on CI's Bun 1.3.1: 114 passed.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, and `bun run format:check`: passed (existing Biome configuration warnings).
- The regression assertion fails with the production change removed.
- Independent measurement across 144 rotated/translated variants: largest observed shortfall below 9e-15 mm. This is a measured sample, not a universal numerical bound.

title: Reproduce polygon board-edge clearance rounding in a TSX snapshot
description: Reproduces a bug where a polygon board with a copper-pour edge margin produces copper slightly inside the clearance, verifying the clearance check error with a comprehensive test.
body:
A 49-point polygon board with a 0.2 mm copper-pour edge margin produces copper slightly inside that clearance. The TSX snapshot displays the actual clearance-check error plus separate required and measured labels: `0.200000000000 mm` versus `0.199998922476 mm`.

The test measures the emitted copper vertices against the board edges, asserts `toBeCloseTo(0.19999892247629383, 12)`, verifies that the gap is below `0.2 - 1e-9`, and confirms that the clearance check reports one error. This records the current bug without changing production code.

Uses the existing `runSolverAndRenderToSvg` helper to exercise the local solver.

Reproduces https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/5301. The fix is stacked in #150.

body:
